state_program_name: Health Care Service Firm (HCSF) registration with the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs (N.J.S.A. 34:8-45.1; N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13 and 13:45B-14), staffed by Board of Nursing-certified Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CHHAs); Medicaid personal care through NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS and the Personal Preference Program (PPP); private-pay home care

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates as a New Jersey Health Care Service Firm (HCSF) registered with the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs (N.J.S.A. 34:8-45.1; N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13 and 13:45B-14). It covers care delivered by Board of Nursing-certified Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CHHAs) under registered nurse supervision. The manual applies to three lines of business:

- **Private-pay home care**
- **Medicaid personal care through NJ FamilyCare:** Personal Care Assistant (PCA) services, Managed Long Term Services and Supports (MLTSS) and the Personal Preference Program (PPP)
- **Placement and employment of CHHAs** by the agency

The manual is meant to:

1. Put into writing the clinical, personnel and administrative practices that the Division's *Best Practices for Health Care Service Firms* (April 15, 2014) describes. Those practices are advisory. The binding rules cited in this manual control wherever the two differ.
2. Make sure daily operations follow the binding rules on placement and delegation, plans of care, patient information, ID tags and prohibited acts (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.6, 13:45B-13.7, 13:45B-14.7 and 13:45B-14.9).
3. Give staff, clients, payers, the Division and the accrediting body a consistent account of what **[AGENCY NAME]** does and why.
4. Support the accreditation that an HCSF must obtain from a NJ Department of Human Services-recognized accrediting body within 12 months of registration (P.L. 2014, c.29; P.L. 2018, c.48). Evidence of that accreditation is required at renewal (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5).

This manual is not legal advice. Where it summarizes a rule, the rule itself governs.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**Organization.** The manual follows the order of the Division's *Best Practices for Health Care Service Firms*:

- **Part II: Clinical**
- **Part III: Personnel**
- **Part IV: Administrative**

Policies that carry a binding rule (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.6, 13.7, 14.7 and 14.9, and the Medicaid PCA rules at N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.4, 3.5 and 3.8) are cross-referenced to that rule in the text.

**Finding the policy for a requirement.** Use **Appendix A**. It lists every official item and shows the policy section that satisfies it. Surveyors, accreditors and auditors can use it to go from a requirement to the matching policy and procedure.

**Customize before adopting.** This is a template. Before use:

1. Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and other bracketed field (addresses, titles, names of the practitioner supervisor and administrator, payer lists, and so on) with the agency's own information.
2. Edit each policy so it matches what **[AGENCY NAME]** actually does. Delete or adapt any line of business the agency does not offer (private-pay, PCA, MLTSS or PPP). A policy the agency does not follow is a compliance risk.
3. Have counsel or a qualified compliance advisor review the customized manual.

**Adopt.** The governing body (owner, board of directors or equivalent) must formally adopt the manual. Record the adoption date, the approver and the version number on the adoption page.

**Keep current.**
- Review the manual at least annually and whenever a rule, payer requirement, accreditation standard or agency practice changes.
- Several items are in flux and need confirmation with the Division (see the Regulatory Framework section): P.L. 2026, c.45 (registration expiration date), the status of the financial-audit provisions of N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5A, and current fee amounts.
- Keep a revision log. Retire superseded versions but archive them.

**Train staff.**
- Give every employee, including CHHAs, supervising nurses, office and intake staff, and managers, the policies that apply to their role. Do this at hire and again when policies change.
- Document the training: who was trained, on what, when, and by whom.
- Keep the manual available to all staff, and available for inspection by the Division and the accrediting body.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

### Governing statutes and rules

**HCSF registration and operation (NJ Division of Consumer Affairs)**

- **N.J.S.A. 34:8-45.1**: Defines a health care service firm as an agency that places or arranges placement of personnel for health care, companion or personal care services. Such a firm must register with the Division of Consumer Affairs.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.2**: Definitions used in the HCSF subchapter.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3**: Initial registration requirements. These include ownership and management disclosures, criminal-conviction certifications, a bond (waivable at a net worth of $100,000 or more), and disclosure of other-state licenses. Changes to application information must be reported to the Division in writing within 30 calendar days.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5**: Registration renewal, including evidence of accreditation.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5A**: Financial statements, audits and reports, with a July 1 annual financial-statement deadline. Some audit provisions were reported as suspended. Confirm their current status with the Division.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.6**: Prohibited acts, such as operating or advertising before registration and charging fees to employees.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.7**: Information for patient/employers. It covers ID tags and delivery of the Board of Nursing's Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7**: Homemaker-home health aides and agencies. It covers placing only actively certified employee CHHAs and delegation by the supervisor.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9**: Duties relating to placements in home care settings. It covers plans of care, 30-day supervisor inquiries, and 60-day in-home evaluations.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-7.1**: Annual registration fee, cited as $500 per primary location through a secondary source. Confirm the current fee on the Division's portal.
- **P.L. 2014, c.29** and **P.L. 2018, c.48**: Accreditation by a NJ Department of Human Services-recognized accrediting body within 12 months of registration, with evidence required at renewal.
- **P.L. 2026, c.45**: Reported to move the annual registration expiration from June 30 to September 30. The source is a secondary summary and Division implementation guidance was pending. **Confirm with the Division.**

**CHHA certification and training (NJ Board of Nursing)**

- **N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2**: Definition of homemaker-home health aide. A NJ RN supervises the certified HHA and the program of care.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.4**: Homemaker-home health aide training program requirements: at least 76 hours (60 classroom, 16 clinical), with Board approval before a program starts. The text came from the Board's 2019 Training Book. Confirm that the current code is unchanged.
- **N.J.S.A. 45:11-24.3 et seq.**: Criminal history background check required before HHA certification.
- **N.J.A.C. 13:37-5.5**: Board of Nursing fees, including the HHA certification application fee. Confirm current amounts with the Board.

**Medicaid / NJ FamilyCare personal care**

- **N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.4**: Certification of need for PCA services by a physician or practitioner, at initial application and annually.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.5**: Duties of the registered professional nurse. These include the plan of care, supervisory visits at least every 60 days, and the first visit within 48 hours of the start of service.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.8**: Limitations on PCA services, including excluded settings, family-member limits, the 40-hour weekly maximum, and no carry-over of unused units.
- **NJ SPA 24-0013**: State plan fee-for-service PCA rate ($26.68/hour, T1019 per 15-minute unit, effective 7/1/2024). MCO rates are contracted and not public.
- **NJ SPA 22-0005**: 1915(j) self-directed PCA reimbursement methodology (Personal Preference Program).
- **21st Century Cures Act §12006(a)**: Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) for Medicaid personal care and home health services delivered in the home. NJ's EVV aggregator is HHAeXchange.

This list reflects the research available when the manual was prepared. Several items were carried from secondary sources and the rule text was not re-read. The NJ DHS-recognized accreditation standards and the Medicaid PCA, MLTSS and PPP program manuals were not reviewed, so requirements found only in those sources are not captured here. Verify all cites against the current official text, and add payer-contract and accreditor requirements during customization.

### Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, Regulated Business Section** | Registers and regulates HCSFs. Receives applications through the NJ Regulated Business Licensure Portal. | Phone: (973) 504-6370; Email: regulatedbusiness@dca.njoag.gov; Web: https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov; Portal: https://rgbportal.dca.njoag.gov/ |
| **NJ Board of Nursing (Division of Consumer Affairs)** | Certifies and regulates CHHAs and approves CHHA training programs. | Phone: 973-504-6430 (Call Center, Mon–Fri 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.); Web: https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/hhh/Pages/General-Questions.aspx |
| **NJ Department of Human Services, Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services (DMAHS)** | Administers NJ FamilyCare, including PCA, the Personal Preference Program and MLTSS through managed care organizations. | Web: https://www.nj.gov/humanservices/dmahs/individuals-families/familycare/mltss/ |
| **County Area Agency on Aging – Aging and Disability Resource Connection (ADRC)** | Intake and screening for adults 21+ seeking MLTSS. | Web: https://www.nj.gov/humanservices/dmahs/individuals-families/familycare/mltss/ (contact your county ADRC) |
| **NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development** | Employer unemployment, disability and family leave contributions; state minimum wage. | Web: https://www.nj.gov/labor/ea/employer-services/rate-info |

### Official policy checklist and review documents

New Jersey does not publish a single official checklist or form listing the written policies an HCSF must have. The registration package (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3) covers application paperwork only. Policies are not submitted through the licensure portal. The documents this manual is built against are:

1. **Best Practices for Health Care Service Firms** (NJ Office of the Attorney General, Division of Consumer Affairs, Regulated Business Section / Board of Nursing; version of April 15, 2014). It has no form number. It is **advisory and non-binding**. It is the only official Division document that lists the policy content a home care HCSF should have in writing. Its three parts (II Clinical, III Personnel, IV Administrative) set the structure of this manual. Where it conflicts with or exceeds N.J.S.A. 34:8-43 et seq. or N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.1 et seq., the statute and rules control.
2. **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.7**, Information for patient/employers (ID tags and the Consumer Guide).
3. **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7**, Homemaker-home health aides and agencies (placement and delegation).
4. **N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.6**, Prohibited acts.

N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3 (initial registration) was reviewed, but it lists only application paperwork, so it is not mapped to policies.

**Appendix A** maps every official item above to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to confirm coverage during Division inspection, accreditation survey and internal audit.

### Customization, adoption, currency and training

- **Customize.** Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and bracketed field, and tailor each policy to the agency's actual operations and lines of business.
- **Adopt.** The governing body must formally adopt the manual and record the date.
- **Keep current.** Review at least annually and whenever rules change. Pending items include the P.L. 2026, c.45 registration-date change, the status of N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5A audit provisions, and Division rule updates.
- **Train.** Train all staff on the policies relevant to their roles at hire and on every material revision, and keep training records.
- **Make available.** Keep the manual accessible for inspection by the Division and the accrediting body.

citations.title: Health care service firm definition and enabling statute
citations.requirement: Defines a health care service firm as an agency that places or arranges placement of personnel for health care, companion or personal care services. A firm that does this must register with the Division of Consumer Affairs (DCA). Statute text was not fetched in this pass. This is carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Definitions (health care service firms)
citations.requirement: Defines the terms used in the HCSF subchapter. Used to confirm that the firm is in scope. Carried from the fact-checked research. Rule text was not re-read.

citations.title: Initial registration requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Register on Director-provided forms. The package includes the firm and trade names, each primary location, officers, directors and principals, owners of 10% or more, and managing agents. It also includes a criminal-conviction certification from each officer, director, principal or owner (N.J.S.A. 34:8-44), a $10,000 bond, and a list of licenses held in other states with any actions taken. The Director may waive the bond for an entity with a net worth of $100,000 or more, shown by a CPA or licensed-accountant certified financial report. (b) Give the owner and managing-agent information before any change in ownership or management. (c) Report any change to application information to the Section in writing within 30 calendar days. (d) If an officer, director, principal or owner is convicted after filing, obtain a new affidavit and file it within 30 days of the conviction.

citations.title: Registration renewal
citations.requirement: Renewal requires evidence of accreditation (in effect from May 21, 2019). Financial statements and audits under 13.5A are submitted with the renewal. Taken from the fact-checked research (50 N.J.R. 1299). Full current text was not re-read.

citations.title: Financial statements, audits, and reports
citations.requirement: (a) Submit a financial statement for the prior calendar year by July 1 each year. It must match the firm's State tax filing and be filed with the renewal. It must show assets, liabilities, gross income, operating expenses, and money received for NJ Medicaid PCA services. (b)-(c) A firm that received more than $250,000 in NJ Medicaid PCA revenue in the relevant year must file a periodic audit. (d) A firm with $10 million or more in gross income must file an audit. (e)-(f) A firm with less than $250,000 in PCA revenue and $1 million to under $10 million in gross income must file a report that includes a review by a NJ-licensed CPA. (j) Audits must have an unqualified opinion plus compliance and financial components. The law-firm summary in the research reports (b)-(e) as suspended, so confirm the current status with DCA.

citations.title: Prohibited acts
citations.requirement: An HCSF shall not: (1) recruit or advertise for staff, offer services, or contract with a facility before obtaining registration; (2) charge a fee or liquidated damages to an employee or in connection with employment, unless it also holds an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2; (3) prevent an employee by contract from working for others, and any fee charged on that basis also requires an employment agency license; (4) knowingly send employees to, or keep serving, a facility not under NLRB jurisdiction where a strike or lockout is in progress, to replace strikers.

citations.title: Information for patient/employers
citations.requirement: (a) Every certified HHA or regulated professional must wear an ID tag at all times while giving care. The tag shows first name or initial, full surname, the certification or licensure level and a photograph. Letters must be equal in size and at least 1/4 inch. The tag must be at least as large as any other ID worn. (b)-(c) Give each patient/employer the Board of Nursing's Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides at least 24 hours before services. (d) The patient may waive the 24-hour timing in writing. The firm keeps the waiver for at least 2 years and must still provide the guide before services begin.

citations.title: Homemaker-home health aides and agencies
citations.requirement: (a) An agency must be licensed as an HCSF to place certified HHAs. (b) It may refer or place only actively certified HHAs it employs. (c) An HHA may perform only tasks delegated by, or directed by, the health care practitioner supervisor. (d) The supervisor must ensure the HHA demonstrates competence in each delegated task. (e) The supervisor must document in the patient's record every task delegated.

citations.title: Duties relating to placements in home care settings
citations.requirement: (a) Before placement, an appropriately licensed person must evaluate the patient's needs and write a plan of care. The preparer signs it with their license designation. (b) Placements must match the level of care in the plan. (c)-(d) At least once in every 30-day period of service, the supervisor inquires whether the plan is adequate and whether it is being carried out, and records the responses. (e) If the plan needs revision, a licensed person must reassess it immediately. (f) If the plan is not being carried out properly, the agency must take corrective action immediately. (g) The supervisor makes an on-site, in-home evaluation of the plan at least once in every 60-day period. (h) The agency keeps the original and any revised plan and gives copies to the patient or representative.

citations.title: Certification of need for personal care assistant services
citations.requirement: A physician or practitioner must certify the need for PCA services in writing, at the initial application and annually. Taken from the fact-checked research. The full text was not re-read.

citations.title: Duties of the registered professional nurse (PCA)
citations.requirement: The RN assesses the beneficiary and prepares the plan of care consistent with the physician/practitioner certification. This is done at the start of service and never later than 48 hours after it. The plan lists tasks, hours, goals and the beneficiary's strengths and family needs. It is dated and signed by the PCA and the RN. The RN directly supervises the PCA in the home during the PCA's assigned time. The minimum is one visit every 60 days, with the first initiated within 48 hours of the start of service. Extra visits are made for a new PCA, nurse delegation or changed needs. With multiple PCAs, visits rotate until all staff are assessed on each covered shift. For beneficiaries in a managed care plan, the plan completes the State PCA Assessment tool and authorizes hours.

citations.title: Limitations on personal care assistant services
citations.requirement: (a) No reimbursement in listed settings, including assisted living, nursing facilities, hospitals and adult day health. (b) PCA services by a family member are not covered, except under the Personal Preference Program. No exceptions for a spouse, legal guardian or parent of a minor. Other relatives may get case-by-case exceptions requested by the agency. In that case the PCA must be a currently certified HHA, an employee of the requesting agency, and directly supervised by that agency's RN. (c) PCA is not authorized for respite, stand-alone supervision, companionship, child care, parenting tasks, mental-health service needs, non-functional diagnoses, acute short-term conditions or non-hands-on-only needs. (d) No reimbursement if the PCA lives in the beneficiary's home. (g) Maximum of 40 hours per calendar work week, prior authorized. (h) For two or more beneficiaries in one residence, combine individual hands-on hours with group hours for household tasks. (i) Unused units cannot be carried over.

citations.title: Homemaker-home health aide training program (as reproduced in the Board of Nursing Training Book, rev. 6/13/19)
citations.requirement: Training is at least 76 hours: 60 classroom plus 16 clinical in a skills lab or patient care setting. Class size is at most 30 students per instructor. Clinical supervision is by an RN at no more than 10 aides per RN. Board of Nursing written approval is required before the program starts. The Board will not certify an applicant until a criminal history check clears. Confirm that the current code version is unchanged from the 2019 Training Book.

citations.title: Definition of homemaker-home health aide (as quoted in the Training Book)
citations.requirement: An HHA is employed by a home care services agency. Under RN supervision, the HHA follows a delegated nursing regimen or performs delegated tasks consistent with N.J.A.C. 13:37-6.2. A NJ RN must supervise the certified HHA and the program of care delivered.

citations.title: Criminal history background check for HHA certification (as cited in the Training Book)
citations.requirement: All initial HHA applicants must undergo a criminal history background check. The Board of Nursing will not certify an applicant until it determines that no disqualifying criminal history record exists in FBI or NJ State Police files.

citations.title: HCSF accreditation within 12 months of registration
citations.requirement: An HCSF must obtain accreditation from a NJ Department of Human Services-recognized accrediting body within 12 months of registration. Carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Act concerning health care service firms and homemaker-home health aides (accreditation)
citations.requirement: Reinforces the accreditation requirement. Evidence of accreditation is required at renewal. Carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: 2026 HCSF law (signed July 22, 2026)
citations.requirement: Moves the annual registration expiration from June 30 to September 30. Registrations that had already renewed for 2026-2027 are extended to Sept. 30, 2027. DCA implementation guidance was pending. The source is a secondary law-firm summary, so confirm with DCA.

citations.title: State plan personal care services rate
citations.requirement: Fee-for-service PCA rate of $26.68/hour (T1019, 15-minute unit), effective 7/1/2024. MCO rates are contracted and not public. Carried from the research.

citations.title: 1915(j) self-directed PCA reimbursement methodology
citations.requirement: Sets the payment methodology for self-directed PCA services (Personal Preference Program). Carried from the research.

citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification mandate
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care and home health services delivered in the home. NJ's EVV aggregator is HHAeXchange (per the research). Carried from the research.

citations.requirement: The $500 annual registration fee per primary location is cited through a secondary source. The rule text was not read. Confirm the current fee on the DCA portal.

citations.requirement: Board of Nursing fee schedule, including the HHA certification application fee. The research cites $50, nonrefundable. Confirm on current Board pages.

policies.title: Intake Interview, Initial Assessment and Post-Facility-Discharge Assignments
policies.applies_to: All new clients of [AGENCY NAME] (private-pay, NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS and Personal Preference Program), the DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors, intake staff, the on-call RN and assigned CHHAs
policies.purpose: To make sure every prospective client receives a documented intake interview and an in-person RN assessment before care starts. For clients discharged from a facility, to make sure an RN is responsible for delegating care during the first 24-48 hours until the designated RN completes the in-person assessment. This protects clients and ensures a CHHA is placed only against a nursing assessment and plan of care.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is registered as a Health Care Service Firm (HCSF) and places only actively certified Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CHHAs) whom it employs (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(a)-(b), citation C8). Before a CHHA is placed, an appropriately licensed person evaluates the client's needs and writes a plan of care (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(a), citation C9). This policy meets Best Practices §II, Intake Interview and Initial Assessment (item II/Intake): for all assignments other than facility discharges, a registered nurse (RN) conducts an in-person nursing assessment of each client before care starts, to establish a baseline of physical and functional status and the level of services needed. The DON/HCSS assigns a nurse, the office manager or another responsible staff member to interview the client and/or family or significant other (see CLN-02 for required documentation). For facility discharges, the DON/HCSS or the on-call RN takes responsibility for delegating care during the first 24-48 hours, pending the designated RN's in-person assessment. A CHHA performs only tasks delegated or directed by the supervisor (C8). For Medicaid PCA clients, the RN assessment and plan of care are completed at the start of service and no later than 48 hours after it begins (N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.5, citation C11). For clients in a managed care plan (MLTSS), the plan completes the State PCA Assessment tool and authorizes hours (C11); [AGENCY NAME] obtains that authorization and does not substitute its own assessment for it. [AGENCY NAME] provides each client its Notice of Privacy Practices no later than the first service delivery (45 CFR 164.520).

definitions.definition: The first structured conversation, by phone or in person, with the prospective client and/or family or significant other to collect identifying, health and service information (see CLN-02).
A face-to-face assessment of the client in the home by an RN (the DON/HCSS or an assigned Nurse Supervisor) that sets the physical and functional baseline and the level of services (see CLN-03).
A referral in which the client is being discharged from a hospital, rehabilitation facility, nursing facility or similar setting to home and care is needed immediately.
The Director of Nursing / Health Care Services Supervisor, a New Jersey-licensed RN designated by [AGENCY NAME] to direct clinical services.
The assignment by an RN of a specific task to a CHHA after the RN has confirmed the CHHA's competence to perform it (see CLN-05).

procedures: Intake staff receive the referral (client, family, hospital discharge planner, NJ FamilyCare MCO or care manager, or ADRC) and record the date and time received on the Intake Form.

The DON/HCSS assigns a nurse, the office manager or another responsible staff member to conduct the intake interview, and records the assignment on the Intake Form. The interview is held with the client and/or family or significant other.
The interviewer completes the Intake Form following CLN-02 and prints, signs and dates it on the day of the interview.

The interviewer identifies the payer source (private pay, NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS, Personal Preference Program) and whether the referral is a facility discharge. The interviewer notes this on the Intake Form and informs the DON/HCSS the same business day.

The DON/HCSS reviews the intake the same day and confirms that the referral is within [AGENCY NAME]'s scope of services (see CLN-10) and that a qualified, actively certified CHHA employed by [AGENCY NAME] is available (see ADM-04 and ADM-08). If not, the DON/HCSS arranges a referral elsewhere and documents it.

Non-discharge referrals: the DON/HCSS assigns an RN (self or an assigned Nurse Supervisor) to perform the in-person nursing assessment in the client's home. The assessment must be completed before any CHHA care begins. No CHHA is sent to a home before the assessment unless the client is a facility discharge under step 7.

Facility discharges: before the first visit, the DON/HCSS or on-call RN (see ADM-11) reviews the discharge orders and summary, speaks with the discharge planner or family, and decides which tasks, if any, the CHHA may be directed to perform. The DON/HCSS or on-call RN accepts responsibility for delegating care during the first 24-48 hours and documents each delegated task in the client record (CLN-05).

For facility discharges, the designated RN completes the full in-person assessment (CLN-03) and plan of care (CLN-04) within 24-48 hours of the start of service. The DON/HCSS checks on the day after start of service that the visit is scheduled and escalates to the Administrator if it is not.

Medicaid PCA clients: the RN assessment and plan of care are completed at the start of service and no later than 48 hours after service begins (C11). The DON/HCSS confirms that the physician or practitioner certification of need is on file (MED-01) and the first RN supervisory visit is initiated within 48 hours of the start of service (MED-02).

MLTSS clients: the intake worker obtains the MCO's authorization and the State PCA Assessment tool results, notes authorized hours on the Intake Form, and coordinates with the MCO care manager (MED-03).

At or before the first service delivery, office staff or the assessing RN give the client the Notice of Privacy Practices and obtain the written acknowledgment, or document the good-faith attempt (ADM-10, CR-01).
The assessing RN gives the client and family a copy of the Client Rights and Responsibilities, the service agreement and the Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CR-01, ADM-12, ADM-13).

The assessing RN completes the assessment, signs and dates it, and delivers it to the DON/HCSS for the plan of care. The CHHA is scheduled only after the plan of care and the competency demonstration are in place (CLN-04, CLN-06), except as permitted under step 7 or step 9.

The DON/HCSS audits each new client record within 14 days of start of service to verify the intake, assessment, plan and delegation entries are present, timely and signed, and records deficiencies for corrective action under ADM-14.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures sufficient RN and CHHA staff are available to complete assessments before care starts and within 24-48 hours for facility discharges; ensures this policy is followed.

Assigns the intake interviewer; reviews every intake the same day; assigns the assessing RN; takes responsibility for delegation in the first 24-48 hours after a facility discharge or designates the on-call RN to do so.

responsibilities.role: Intake interviewer (nurse, office manager or other designated staff)
responsibilities.duty: Conducts the interview, completes and signs the Intake Form, identifies payer and discharge status and notifies the DON/HCSS.
Conducts the in-person assessment before care starts (or within 24-48 hours for discharges and PCA), writes the plan of care and documents delegation.
Directs and documents delegated care after hours for a facility discharge until the designated RN's assessment is done.

documentation: Referral log with date and time received
Completed and signed Intake Form (CLN-02)
Record of intake assignment by DON/HCSS
Facility discharge orders/summary and the RN delegation entries for the first 24-48 hours
In-person nursing assessment (CLN-03)
Medicaid PCA certification of need and MCO authorization / State PCA Assessment tool results, where applicable
Signed acknowledgment of Notice of Privacy Practices
New-client record audit checklist

policies.title: Intake Interview Documentation
policies.applies_to: Intake interviewers (nurses, office manager and other designated staff), the DON/HCSS and Nurse Supervisors
policies.purpose: To make sure every intake interview is documented on a standard Intake Form that captures the information the RN needs to prepare for assessment and to decide which delegated tasks a CHHA may later perform.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] documents every intake interview on the Intake Form. A CHHA may perform only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(c), citation C8), so intake information supports, and does not replace, the RN's assessment and delegation. The Intake Form contains the following, which meet the Best Practices §II Required Intake Interview Documentation items: (1) II/Intake Documentation 1 - full name of the patient; (2) II/Intake Documentation 2 - date of birth; (3) II/Intake Documentation 3 - gender; (4) II/Intake Documentation 4 - Primary Care Provider and/or other health care professional contact information, including name and phone number; (5) II/Intake Documentation 5 - past medical history, if known; (6) II/Intake Documentation 6 - nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s), if known; (7) II/Intake Documentation 7 - list of medications, if known; (8) II/Intake Documentation 8 - functional status, if known; (9) II/Intake Documentation 9 - family/significant-other contact information, including name, phone number and relationship to the patient; (10) II/Intake Documentation 10 - identification of services in place, additional services needed and collateral contacts, if applicable; and (11) II/Intake Documentation 11 - the printed name, date and signature of the person conducting the intake. If the history, diagnoses, medications or functional status are not known, the Intake Form must show the attempt made to obtain them (who was asked, when and the result). Intake records are protected as protected health information with appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards (45 CFR 164.530(c)).

definitions.definition: The standard [AGENCY NAME] form used to document the intake interview.
A person or organization, such as a physician, discharge planner, MCO care manager, ADRC, clergy or neighbor, who can give information about the client or who provides services to the client.
Services the client already receives, such as home health nursing, therapy, adult day health, meals, or other caregivers.

procedures: Before the interview, the interviewer opens a new Intake Form for the client and records the date, time, referral source and whether the contact is by phone or in person.
The interviewer records the client's full legal name as it appears on the client's identification or insurance card and asks about any other names used.
The interviewer records the client's date of birth and gender and verifies them against the referral document or insurance card where available.

The interviewer records the name, practice and phone number of the client's primary care provider and any other health care professional involved (specialist, home health nurse, therapist, discharge planner).
The interviewer records the name, phone number and relationship to the client of the family member or significant other, and notes whether the person is the client's legal representative.

The interviewer records the client's past medical history, nursing and medical diagnoses or problems, current medication list and functional status (mobility, transfers, bathing, dressing, toileting, eating, cognition, communication) as reported, marking each item 'reported' or 'unknown'.

For any history, diagnoses, medications or functional-status item that is unknown, the interviewer documents the attempt to obtain it (for example, called PCP office [date/time], awaiting records; asked daughter, she does not know) and notifies the assessing RN so it can be followed up at the in-person assessment.
The interviewer records services already in place, additional services the client or family say are needed, and collateral contacts, with their phone numbers, or writes 'none' where not applicable.
The interviewer records the payer source and any MCO/care manager or ADRC contact (see CLN-01 and MED-03).
The interviewer prints his or her name, signs and dates the Intake Form on the day of the interview. Unsigned forms are incomplete and cannot be used to schedule services.
The interviewer delivers the form to the DON/HCSS the same business day for review (CLN-01, step 5).

The DON/HCSS reviews the form for all eleven required elements and returns incomplete forms to the interviewer for correction the same day; corrections are made by dated, initialed addenda, never by erasure or overwriting.

The Intake Form is filed in the client record (REC-01). Paper copies are kept in a locked cabinet and electronic copies in the access-controlled record system, available only to staff who need them (45 CFR 164.530(c); ADM-10).
The DON/HCSS includes a sample of Intake Forms in the quarterly record review under ADM-14 and reports completeness results to the Administrator.

responsibilities.duty: Completes every element of the Intake Form, documents attempts to obtain unknown information, and prints, signs and dates the form.
Reviews each Intake Form for completeness the same business day and assures corrections through addenda.
Uses the intake information and follows up on items marked unknown at the in-person assessment.
Files the form in the client record and maintains record security.

documentation: Completed Intake Form with all eleven required elements
Documentation of attempts to obtain unknown history, diagnoses, medications or functional status
Dated, initialed addenda for any corrections
Collateral contact list
DON/HCSS review notation
Quarterly intake audit results

policies.title: In-Person Nursing Assessment
policies.applies_to: The DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors (NJ-licensed RNs) and all clients of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every client receives a complete, documented in-person nursing assessment, before service starts, that sets a physical and functional baseline and determines which tasks may be delegated to a CHHA.
policies.policy: Before placement, an appropriately licensed person must evaluate the patient's needs and write a plan of care (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(a), citation C9). At [AGENCY NAME] this evaluation is the in-person nursing assessment, performed in the client's home by the DON/HCSS or an assigned Nurse Supervisor (a New Jersey-licensed RN) before service starts, or within 24 to 48 hours for facility discharges (see CLN-01). For Medicaid PCA clients, the RN assessment is completed at the start of service and no later than 48 hours after it (N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.5, citation C11). The assessment is used to decide which tasks may be delegated to the assigned CHHA (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(c), citation C8). The assessment documents the following, which meet the Best Practices §II Required In-Person Assessment Documentation items: II/In-Person Assessment 1 - vital signs (temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure) and a pain assessment, performed by the DON/HCSS or assigned Nurse Supervisor to determine tasks to delegate, before service starts (or within 24 to 48 hours for facility discharges); II/In-Person Assessment 2 - past medical history; II/In-Person Assessment 3 - nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s); II/In-Person Assessment 4 - list of medications; II/In-Person Assessment 5 - functional status; II/In-Person Assessment 6 - psycho-social review relevant to the Plan of Care; II/In-Person Assessment 7 - a systems review (neurologic, musculo-skeletal, integumentary, cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastro-intestinal, genito-urinary); II/In-Person Assessment 8 - nutritional status, including diet; II/In-Person Assessment 9 - home safety review, including fall risk assessment; II/In-Person Assessment 10 - emergency plan; II/In-Person Assessment 11 - advance directives; II/In-Person Assessment 12 - the Primary Care Provider's Certification of Need for Services, if applicable (for Medicaid PCA, a physician or practitioner must certify the need in writing at the initial application and annually, N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.4, citation C10); and II/In-Person Assessment 13 - the date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor conducting the assessment. The preparer signs with his or her license designation (C9). For managed care (MLTSS) clients the MCO completes the State PCA Assessment tool and authorizes hours (C11); [AGENCY NAME]'s assessment is still completed for delegation and plan-of-care purposes. Assessment records are safeguarded as protected health information (45 CFR 164.530(c)).

definitions.definition: A New Jersey-licensed RN assigned by the DON/HCSS to assess clients, write plans of care, delegate tasks and supervise CHHAs.
The client's physical, functional, cognitive and psycho-social status at the start of service against which later changes are measured.
The written certification by a physician or practitioner that the client needs personal care services, required for Medicaid PCA at initial application and annually (C10).
A structured review of the client's history of falls, gait and balance, medications, environmental hazards and other risk factors.
A client's written instructions for health care decisions, such as a living will, health care proxy or Practitioner Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST).

procedures: The DON/HCSS reviews the Intake Form and assigns the assessment to an RN (self or Nurse Supervisor) with a date that is before service start, or within 24-48 hours for facility discharges and no later than 48 hours after start of service for Medicaid PCA.
The RN calls the client or representative to schedule the home visit, confirms who will be present and records the date and time.
On arrival the RN verifies the client's identity, explains the purpose of the assessment, and obtains the client's consent to proceed.
The RN measures and records temperature, pulse, respiration and blood pressure, and conducts and records a pain assessment (location, intensity, character, what relieves it).
The RN reviews and records the past medical history and the nursing and medical diagnoses or problems, comparing them to what was recorded at intake and the referral records.

The RN reviews the medications actually in the home (name, dose, route, frequency, who administers them), compares them to the list at intake and discharge/physician orders, and records discrepancies. Any discrepancy is referred to the prescriber or PCP the same day.
The RN assesses and records functional status (mobility, transfers, bathing, dressing, toileting, continence, eating, cognition, communication, use of equipment).

The RN completes and records the psycho-social review as it relates to the plan of care (living situation, caregiver support, mood, coping, cultural and language needs, risk of abuse, neglect or exploitation).

The RN completes and records the systems review: neurologic, musculo-skeletal, integumentary (including skin condition and pressure injury risk), cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastro-intestinal and genito-urinary.
The RN records nutritional status, including diet orders, restrictions, swallowing and hydration concerns, and weight if available.

The RN walks through the home and completes the home safety review, including a fall risk assessment, noting hazards, equipment needs, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, and pets. Hazards are discussed with the client and recorded with the action agreed.
The RN reviews and records the client's emergency plan: who to call, evacuation needs, the location of medications and emergency contacts, and backup if the CHHA cannot come (SAF-04, CLN-13).

The RN asks about and records advance directives, requests a copy for the record, and notes the location of any POLST or DNR form. The RN does not give legal advice and refers questions to the client's physician or attorney.

The RN obtains and files the PCP's or physician's Certification of Need where applicable. For Medicaid PCA, the RN confirms it is current and will be renewed annually (MED-01). Services that require it are not delivered without it.
The RN records which tasks may be delegated to a CHHA and which must remain with a nurse, and identifies any task for which the assigned CHHA will need a demonstration (CLN-05, CLN-06).

The RN dates and signs the assessment with his or her name and license designation, and submits it to the DON/HCSS within one business day. The DON/HCSS reviews, countersigns if the RN is not the DON/HCSS, and files it in the client record.

The RN uses the assessment to write the plan of care (CLN-04). Findings that need urgent follow-up (for example, an unsafe home, a suspected abuse, a medication problem) are reported to the DON/HCSS immediately (SAF-01, SAF-02).

responsibilities.duty: Assigns and reviews each assessment; ensures timeframes are met; performs assessments personally as needed.
Completes all thirteen assessment elements, signs with license designation, and uses findings to decide tasks to delegate.
Schedule the visit and confirm the Certification of Need and MCO authorization are on file or requested.
Provides RN capacity and ensures timeframes are monitored.

documentation: Signed and dated in-person nursing assessment with license designation of the Nurse Supervisor
Vital signs and pain assessment record
Medication list and discrepancy follow-up notes
Fall risk assessment and home safety review
Emergency plan and advance directive documentation
Physician/PCP Certification of Need (Medicaid PCA, annually) and MCO authorization / State PCA Assessment tool
Task delegation determination (CLN-05)

policies.title: Plan of Care Development, Signatures and Copies
policies.applies_to: The DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors, assigned CHHAs, clients and their families or representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure every client has a written, signed plan of care developed by a licensed nurse from the in-person assessment; that placements match the plan's level of care; and that the plan is available to the client, family and staff.
policies.policy: Before placement, an appropriately licensed person evaluates the patient's needs and writes a plan of care, and the preparer signs it with his or her license designation (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(a), citation C9). At [AGENCY NAME] the DON/HCSS or assigned Nurse Supervisor (RN) develops the plan of care from the in-person assessment before service starts, or within 24 to 48 hours for facility discharges (item II/Plan of Care 1). For Medicaid PCA clients, the RN prepares the plan consistent with the physician/practitioner certification at the start of service and no later than 48 hours after; it lists tasks, hours, goals and the beneficiary's strengths and family needs, and is dated and signed by the PCA and the RN (N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.5, citation C11). Placements must match the level of care in the plan (C9(b)). For clients in MLTSS, the plan is consistent with the person-centered service plan developed by the MCO care manager (42 CFR 441.301(c)). The plan of care states: II/Plan of Care 1 - days and hours of service; II/Plan of Care 2 - nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s); II/Plan of Care 3 - tasks to be performed by employees and the licensure/registration status of the assigned employees (RNs, LPNs, CHHAs, unlicensed assistive personnel and therapists); II/Plan of Care 4 - the frequency of the tasks; II/Plan of Care 5 - short-term and long-term goals for patient care and discharge; II/Plan of Care 6 - the specific changes in patient status that must be reported to the Nurse Supervisor; II/Plan of Care 7 - the date and signature of the nurse who assessed the patient and developed or modified the plan; II/Plan of Care 8 - the date and signature of the patient and/or family/significant other; II/Plan of Care 9 - the date and signature of the employee assigned at the start of service; and II/Plan of Care 10 - the date and signature of the assigned employee at each reassessment and whenever the plan changes. A copy of the plan is kept in the office and at the patient's residence and is available to the patient, family/significant others and agency employees. The agency keeps the original and any revised plan and gives copies to the patient or representative (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(h), C9).

definitions.definition: The written document that states the client's needs, services, tasks, frequency, staff, goals and reporting parameters, developed by an RN from the in-person assessment.
The type of caregiver required by the plan (for example, CHHA under RN supervision, or a nurse). A placement must match this.
A change in the client's condition, function, behavior or environment that the CHHA must tell the Nurse Supervisor, listed by the RN on the plan for that client.
A person legally authorized to act for the client, such as a guardian or health care agent, or a family member or significant other participating with the client's consent.

procedures: The DON/HCSS or Nurse Supervisor drafts the plan of care from the in-person assessment (CLN-03) and the physician/practitioner orders or Certification of Need and MCO authorization, as applicable, before service starts (or within 24-48 hours for facility discharges; for Medicaid PCA at the start of service and no later than 48 hours after).
The RN lists the days and hours of service. For NJ FamilyCare clients the hours may not exceed those authorized by the MCO or DMAHS (MED-01, MED-03).
The RN lists nursing and medical diagnoses or problems from the assessment.

The RN lists each task to be performed, the person or category performing it (RN, LPN, CHHA, unlicensed assistive personnel, therapist) and each assigned employee's license or certification status, and confirms the level of care matches the staff assigned (CLN-05, ADM-08).
The RN lists the frequency of each task (for example, bathing, three times weekly; meal preparation, daily).
The RN writes short-term and long-term goals for care and for discharge or transition from services, including the client's strengths and family needs for Medicaid PCA.

The RN lists the specific changes in status that the CHHA must report to the Nurse Supervisor (for example, falls, new skin breakdown, confusion, refusal of food or medication, shortness of breath) and the phone number to call, including the on-call number (CLN-13, ADM-11).
The RN signs and dates the plan with his or her license designation.

The RN reviews the plan with the client and/or family/significant other, answers questions, makes changes the client requests that are safe and within scope, and obtains the client's or representative's dated signature.

The RN reviews the plan with the assigned CHHA, completing CLN-06 where needed, and obtains the CHHA's dated signature before the CHHA starts care. The CHHA signs again at each reassessment and whenever the plan is changed.

The RN gives a copy to the client or representative at the time of signing. A copy is placed in the client's home, in the location agreed with the client, and a copy is kept in the office. The original and every revised version are kept in the client record (C9(h)).

At each 30-day contact and 60-day in-person evaluation the Nurse Supervisor reviews whether the plan is adequate and being carried out (CLN-08). If it needs revision, a licensed person reassesses it immediately (C9(e)). If it is not being carried out properly, the agency takes corrective action immediately (C9(f)).

When the plan is revised, the RN dates and signs the revised plan, obtains new signatures from the client/representative and the assigned CHHA, replaces the home copy and files the old version in the record marked 'superseded' with the date.

The office manager checks on the next business day that all three signatures and dates are on every new or revised plan, and reports missing signatures to the DON/HCSS, who obtains them within three business days. Missing signatures are tracked in the quality review (ADM-14).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures every client has a signed plan before service starts (or within the 24-48 hour timeframe) and that placements match the plan's level of care.
Writes, signs and revises the plan; reviews it with the client and CHHA; gives copies.
Reads, signs and follows the plan; reports changes listed on it; keeps the home copy available.
Reviews, helps shape and signs the plan; keeps the home copy.
Maintains the original and revised plans and verifies signatures.

documentation: Original signed plan of care and all revised plans
Signatures and dates of the RN, client/representative and assigned CHHA at start, reassessment and each change
List of reportable changes in status
Proof of delivery of a copy to the client or representative
Home copy location note
Physician/practitioner certification and MCO authorization where applicable
Signature compliance log

policies.title: Nurse Delegation and Practitioner Supervisor Duties
policies.applies_to: The DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors (RNs), and all CHHAs employed by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that CHHAs perform only tasks that the health care practitioner supervisor has delegated or directed, that the supervisor ensures competence in each delegated task, and that every delegation is documented in the client's record.
policies.policy: A CHHA is employed by a home care services agency and, under RN supervision, follows a delegated nursing regimen or performs delegated tasks; a New Jersey RN must supervise the certified CHHA and the program of care delivered (N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2, citation C14). This policy meets N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(c): a homemaker-home health aide employed by [AGENCY NAME] performs only tasks delegated by, or directed by, the health care practitioner supervisor (citation C8). This policy meets N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(d): the health care practitioner supervisor ensures that the aide demonstrates competence to perform the client care that is delegated. This policy meets N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(e): the health care practitioner supervisor documents in the patient's record every task delegated to a homemaker-home health aide. At [AGENCY NAME] the health care practitioner supervisor is a New Jersey-licensed RN (the DON/HCSS or an assigned Nurse Supervisor). Delegation is consistent with the New Jersey Nurse Practice Act and Board of Nursing rules. A CHHA who is asked by anyone, including a client or family member, to perform a task that is not on the plan of care or has not been delegated must decline and call the Nurse Supervisor. [AGENCY NAME] places only actively certified CHHAs whom it employs (C8, N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(b)).

definitions.definition: The New Jersey-licensed RN at [AGENCY NAME] responsible for delegating tasks to, directing and supervising the CHHA and the program of care.
The RN's assignment of a specific task to a CHHA for a specific client after assessing the client and the CHHA's competence, and with instructions for performing and reporting.
A task the supervisor instructs the CHHA to perform in the course of the plan of care, including an instruction given by phone and documented afterward.
Demonstrated ability to perform a task safely and correctly for the particular client.

procedures: During the in-person assessment (CLN-03) the Nurse Supervisor decides, task by task, whether the task is appropriate to delegate for this client, considering the client's stability, complexity, risk and the task's scope (CLN-10, CLN-11).
The Nurse Supervisor lists each delegated task on the plan of care (CLN-04) with its frequency, the CHHA assigned, specific instructions and what the CHHA must report.

Before the CHHA performs any task for the first time with the client, the Nurse Supervisor confirms the CHHA's competence by observing the CHHA perform it or by in-person description and demonstration (CLN-06), and records the result.
If the CHHA cannot show competence, the Nurse Supervisor does not delegate the task, provides training and re-checks, or assigns another CHHA or a nurse. The decision is documented.

The Nurse Supervisor documents every delegated task in the client record on the day of delegation: task, date, instructions given, CHHA's name and certification number, how competence was shown, and the Nurse Supervisor's name, signature and license designation.

If the supervisor delegates or directs a task by phone (for example, a change in the client's needs), the supervisor documents the order in the client record the same day, and the CHHA writes the change on the weekly activity record (CLN-07). Written plan revision follows under CLN-04.

The CHHA performs only the tasks listed on the plan of care or delegated or directed by the supervisor. The CHHA declines any other task, explains politely that it is not on the plan, and calls the Nurse Supervisor or on-call RN (ADM-11).
A CHHA must refuse a delegation he or she cannot competently carry out, and must tell the Nurse Supervisor immediately. A CHHA is never disciplined for a good-faith refusal on these grounds.
The Nurse Supervisor reviews each CHHA's weekly activity records (CLN-07) to confirm the tasks documented match those delegated, and follows up on any task done that was not delegated.

At the 30-day contact and 60-day in-person visit (CLN-08), and during supervisory observation (CLN-09), the Nurse Supervisor re-confirms the delegated tasks remain appropriate and the CHHA remains competent, and adds, changes or withdraws delegations as the client's condition changes.
When the client's condition changes (CLN-13), the Nurse Supervisor reassesses and immediately withdraws any delegation that is no longer safe, records the withdrawal and informs the CHHA and client.

The DON/HCSS audits a sample of client records each quarter to confirm that every delegated task is documented and each CHHA's competence for that task is recorded, and reports findings to the Administrator (ADM-14).

responsibilities.duty: Serves as health care practitioner supervisor and oversees all delegation by Nurse Supervisors; audits delegation records.
Decides what to delegate, ensures and documents competence, and documents every delegated task in the client record.
Performs only delegated or directed tasks; refuses and reports any task outside the plan or beyond his or her competence.
Ensures sufficient RN supervision is available so delegation is never made without a supervising RN.

documentation: Delegation entry for every task in the client record (date, task, instructions, CHHA, competence method, RN signature and license)
Plan of care listing delegated tasks (CLN-04)
Competence demonstration records (CLN-06, PER-08)
Records of withdrawn delegations
Telephone direction notes
Quarterly delegation audit

policies.title: Competency Check Before Services Start in a New Client Home
policies.applies_to: Nurse Supervisors (RNs), the DON/HCSS and all CHHAs assigned to a new client
policies.purpose: To make sure that, before services start in a new client's home, the assigned CHHA understands and can perform the delegated tasks for that client, regardless of the CHHA's experience.
policies.policy: This policy meets Best Practices §II, Competency Evaluation of Assigned CHHAs Prior to the Start of Services (item II/Competency Evaluation Prior to Start). Before services start in a new client's home, each assigned CHHA receives an in-person description and/or demonstration of the delegated tasks from the RN, regardless of experience level. The RN assures that the CHHA has the requisite skills and may refuse to delegate to a CHHA who lacks the competencies. A CHHA has a duty to refuse a delegation he or she cannot competently carry out. This is consistent with the requirement that the supervisor ensure the aide demonstrates competence to perform the client care that is delegated (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(d), citation C8) and that a New Jersey RN supervises the certified CHHA and the program of care (N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2, citation C14). The demonstration is documented in the client record and in the CHHA's personnel file.

definitions.definition: A face-to-face explanation by the RN of how a task is to be done for this client, with the RN or the CHHA demonstrating it and the CHHA return-demonstrating where the task requires a skill.
Any client residence in which the assigned CHHA has not previously been delegated tasks for this client, including a returning client after a hospital stay or a significant change in condition.
The knowledge and hands-on abilities needed to perform each delegated task safely for this client, including client-specific preferences, equipment and precautions.

procedures: After writing the plan of care (CLN-04), the Nurse Supervisor identifies the CHHA to be assigned and confirms that the CHHA is actively certified and employed by [AGENCY NAME] (PER-03, PER-11).

The Nurse Supervisor schedules an in-person meeting with the CHHA in the client's home (or, where the client agrees, in another setting for tasks that do not require the home) before the first scheduled visit.

The Nurse Supervisor reviews the plan of care with the CHHA task by task, including frequency, client preferences, precautions, equipment, the changes the CHHA must report, and who to call (CLN-04, ADM-11).

For each delegated task, the Nurse Supervisor describes and, where the task involves a skill (for example, transfers, use of a mechanical lift, assistance with ambulation, incontinence care, positioning, bathing for a client with skin concerns, specific medication-reminder routines), demonstrates it, and then watches the CHHA return-demonstrate it. This applies to every CHHA regardless of experience level or years of work.
The Nurse Supervisor asks the CHHA to describe what he or she would do if the client has the issues listed in the plan (for example, a fall, shortness of breath) and corrects any misunderstanding.

The Nurse Supervisor decides whether the CHHA has the requisite skills for each task. If the CHHA lacks a skill, the Nurse Supervisor does not delegate that task, provides coaching and repeats the demonstration, or assigns a different CHHA or another level of staff. The RN may refuse to delegate to a CHHA who lacks the competencies.

The Nurse Supervisor tells the CHHA that the CHHA has a duty to refuse a delegation he or she cannot competently carry out and must call the Nurse Supervisor or on-call RN immediately; the CHHA acknowledges this by signature.

The Nurse Supervisor documents in the client record the date, tasks described or demonstrated, the CHHA's name and certification number, the result for each task (competent / needs training / not delegated) and the Nurse Supervisor's signature and license designation (CLN-05).
The Nurse Supervisor places a copy of the competency record in the CHHA's personnel file (PER-08, PER-09) and the CHHA signs the plan of care (CLN-04) only after the demonstration.

No CHHA begins care in the home until the demonstration is documented. In a facility discharge where the assessment is delayed under CLN-01, the DON/HCSS or on-call RN gives the CHHA the instructions for the first-visit tasks directly, limits delegation to tasks the CHHA is competent to perform, and documents it.

If a different CHHA is substituted (CLN-12), the Nurse Supervisor repeats this demonstration with the substitute before the substitute starts care, or limits the substitute to tasks previously shown to be within the substitute's competence, and documents the decision.
The Nurse Supervisor re-checks competence at the first observation visit and whenever the plan changes to add a new task (CLN-08, CLN-09).

responsibilities.duty: Describes and/or demonstrates the delegated tasks in person before services start; decides whether the CHHA is competent and documents the decision.
Ensures that no CHHA starts in a new home without the documented demonstration; resolves disputes about CHHA readiness.
Attends the demonstration, asks questions, return-demonstrates, and refuses any delegation he or she cannot competently perform.
Does not schedule a CHHA to a new client's home until the DON/HCSS or Nurse Supervisor confirms the demonstration is done.

documentation: Client record entry: date, tasks, CHHA name and certification number, competence result, RN signature and license designation
Copy of the competency record in the CHHA personnel file
CHHA acknowledgment of the duty to refuse an incompetent delegation
Plan of care signed by the CHHA after demonstration
Records of any task not delegated and the reason

policies.title: Weekly CHHA Activity Records
policies.applies_to: All Certified Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CHHAs) employed by [AGENCY NAME], Nurse Supervisors, and office staff who file clinical records, for every client (private-pay, NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS and Personal Preference Program).
policies.purpose: To make sure that each CHHA's work in a client's home is recorded every week, that the record shows what was done against the Plan of Care and what was not done, that changes in condition are documented, and that the record is signed, filed and retained.
policies.policy:
Each CHHA prepares and files a weekly activity sheet with [AGENCY NAME] for every client served. This policy meets the Best Practices §II items for Weekly CHHA Activity Records 1 through 5. Under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7, a CHHA performs only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor, and the supervisor documents every delegated task in the patient's record. The weekly sheet shows the CHHA's work against those delegated tasks.

Item 1 (Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 1 — date and time of each patient assignment; weekly activity sheet filed with the HCSF): the sheet records the date and the start and end time of each assignment, and the CHHA files it with the agency each week.

Item 2 (Weekly CHHA Activity Records 2 — activities performed and Plan of Care activities not performed, with reasons): the sheet lists the activities performed. It also lists each Plan of Care activity that was not performed, with the reason.

Item 3 (Weekly CHHA Activity Records 3 — change in condition reported to the Nurse Supervisor and documented by both CHHA and nurse): the CHHA records on the sheet any change in condition and the report to the Nurse Supervisor. The Nurse Supervisor separately documents the report and the response in the clinical record.

Item 4 (Weekly CHHA Activity Records 4 — date and signature of the CHHA): the CHHA signs and dates the sheet.

Item 5 (Weekly CHHA Activity Records 5 — date and signature of patient, family member, significant other or designated party; retention): the client or the client's family member, significant other or designee signs and dates the sheet. Completed sheets are kept with the client's medical record in the office for at least 7 years for an adult client and 21 years for a pediatric client, or longer if the law requires.

The weekly activity sheet is a clinical record. For Medicaid clients it is separate from electronic visit verification (EVV) under 42 USC 1396b(l) and does not replace it (see CLN-12).

definitions.definition: The agency form on which a CHHA records, for one client and one work week, each assignment's date and time, the activities performed, Plan of Care activities not performed with reasons, any change in condition reported, and the required signatures.
A person the client has named, or who is legally authorized, to sign for the client when the client cannot sign. Examples are a family member or significant other.
The New Jersey registered professional nurse who supervises the CHHA and the program of care (see CLN-05).
The written plan prepared by an appropriately licensed person before placement, listing the tasks and services to be provided (see CLN-04).

procedures: At hire and again at first assignment, the Nurse Supervisor trains each CHHA on the weekly activity sheet. Training covers how to record times, activities performed, activities not performed and changes in condition. It also covers who may sign for the client. Training is documented in the personnel record.

At the start of each work week ([DAY OF WEEK]), the scheduler gives or sends each CHHA a blank weekly activity sheet for each assigned client. The sheet is pre-printed with the client name and the Plan of Care task list, or the CHHA is given a copy of the task list.
At each visit, the CHHA records the date and the actual start and end times of the assignment on the sheet before leaving the home.
The CHHA checks off or lists each activity performed during the visit, matching the Plan of Care task list.

For any Plan of Care activity not performed, the CHHA writes the activity and the reason (for example: client refused, client in hospital, supplies unavailable, task not safe). The CHHA does not leave this blank.

If the CHHA observes a change in the client's condition, the CHHA notifies the Nurse Supervisor right away, following CLN-13. The CHHA records on the sheet the change, the date and time of the report, and the Nurse Supervisor's instruction.
The Nurse Supervisor documents the same report and the response in the clinical record on the date received. The two entries are matched when the sheet is reviewed.
At the end of the week, the CHHA signs and dates the sheet.

The CHHA asks the client, or the client's family member, significant other or designated party, to review the sheet and sign and date it. If no one is able to sign, the CHHA writes the reason and notifies the Nurse Supervisor, who follows up with the client or representative.
The CHHA must never sign for the client. The CHHA must never ask a client to sign a blank or incomplete sheet.
The CHHA delivers the completed sheet to the office, or uploads it by [APPROVED METHOD], no later than [DAY AND TIME] following the end of the work week.

Office staff log the receipt date and check each sheet for completeness: dates and times, activities, activities not performed with reasons, change-in-condition entries, CHHA signature and client or designee signature. Staff return any incomplete sheet to the CHHA the same business day.

The Nurse Supervisor reviews each sheet. Any sheet showing tasks not performed, a change in condition or a possible error is reviewed within [TIMEFRAME]. The review is documented in the clinical record.

The Nurse Supervisor compares sheets with the Plan of Care at each 30-day contact and 60-day in-person re-evaluation (CLN-08). The review is used to find tasks the CHHA is not performing, which calls for corrective action.

The completed sheet is filed in the client's medical record in the office. Records are kept at least 7 years for adult clients and 21 years for pediatric clients, or longer if the law requires, per REC-01.

The Administrator or designee audits [NUMBER] sheets per month for completeness and timeliness. Results go to the Quality Assurance program (ADM-14). Repeated late or incomplete sheets are addressed through coaching and, if needed, progressive discipline.

responsibilities.duty: Completes, signs and dates the weekly activity sheet, obtains the client or designee signature, records changes in condition and reports them to the Nurse Supervisor, and submits the sheet on time.
Trains CHHAs on the sheet, documents reported changes in condition in the clinical record, reviews the sheets against the Plan of Care and takes corrective action.
Logs receipt, checks completeness, returns incomplete sheets and files and retains sheets with the medical record.
Ensures records are kept for the required retention periods and that audit results feed the Quality Assurance program.

documentation: Weekly activity sheet (date and time of each assignment, activities performed, activities not performed with reasons, change-in-condition entries, CHHA signature and date, client/designee signature and date)
Nurse Supervisor clinical record entry for each reported change in condition
Sheet receipt log
CHHA training record on the weekly activity sheet
Audit results and any corrective action

policies.title: Periodic Patient Review: 30-Day Contact and 60-Day In-Person Re-evaluation
policies.applies_to: Nurse Supervisors/health care practitioner supervisors, CHHAs and records staff for all clients receiving services, including NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS and Personal Preference Program clients and private-pay clients.
policies.purpose: To make sure that each client's Plan of Care is checked regularly, that the Plan of Care is adequate and being carried out, and that the plan is revised promptly when needs change.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] reviews each client's care on a regular schedule. This policy meets the Best Practices §II Periodic Patient Review and Re-Evaluation items: II/Periodic Review, II/Periodic Review Changes 1-7 and II/Periodic Review Documentation 1-4.

II/Periodic Review: The Nurse Supervisor reviews care records regularly and contacts the patient or significant other at least once in every 30-day period of service to ask whether the plan is adequate and whether it is being carried out. The responses are recorded in the clinical record (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(c)-(d)). The Nurse Supervisor also re-evaluates the client in person, in the home, at least once in every 60-day period (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(g)). The re-evaluation is done sooner when the client's condition warrants, after an interruption of service, hospitalization or facility stay, after a change in condition or functional status, or if the service agreement calls for it. For Medicaid PCA clients, the RN supervises the PCA in the home at least once every 60 days, with the first visit initiated within 48 hours of the start of service. Additional visits are made for a new PCA, nurse delegation or changed needs (N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.5). The 60-day visit satisfies both requirements when it meets each rule's content.

II/Periodic Review Changes 1-7: If the nurse changes the Plan of Care, the documentation states the reasons, based on a review of: (1) nursing and medical diagnoses or problems; (2) changes in vital signs, including temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure and a pain assessment; (3) changes in functional status; (4) psycho-social review relevant to the Plan of Care; (5) nutritional status, including diet; (6) home safety, including a fall risk assessment; and (7) the emergency plan.

II/Periodic Review Documentation 1-4: The re-evaluation record includes (1) the names of any employees present, their licensure status and the skills observed; (2) confirmation that the Plan of Care was reviewed with the CHHA; (3) any communication with the patient, family, significant other or designated party about complaints or problems; and (4) the date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor.

If the plan needs revision, a licensed person reassesses it immediately. If the plan is not being carried out properly, the agency takes corrective action immediately (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(e)-(f)). The agency keeps the original and revised plans and gives copies to the patient or representative (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(h)).

definitions.definition: A review of care records and a contact with the patient or significant other at least once in every 30-day period of service to ask whether the Plan of Care is adequate and being carried out.
An on-site, in-home evaluation of the Plan of Care by the Nurse Supervisor at least once in every 60-day period of service.
An interruption of service, hospitalization or facility stay, change in condition or functional status, or a service-agreement term that calls for an earlier re-evaluation.
The New Jersey registered professional nurse (or other health care practitioner supervisor permitted by rule) responsible for the client's Plan of Care and for supervising the CHHA.

procedures: At the start of service, the Nurse Supervisor enters in the scheduling system the due dates for each client's 30-day contacts and 60-day in-person re-evaluations. The dates are counted from the start of service and from each completed contact. For Medicaid PCA clients, the first RN supervisory visit is initiated within 48 hours of the start of service, as scheduled under MED-02.
The system generates a report each week of reviews due within the next 14 days. The Director of Nursing/HCSS checks it and reassigns any review that is at risk of being late.
Before each review, the Nurse Supervisor reads the weekly activity sheets (CLN-07), prior visit notes, incident reports and any complaints since the last review.

At least once in every 30-day period, the Nurse Supervisor contacts the patient or significant other. Contact is by phone, video or in person. The Nurse Supervisor asks (a) whether the Plan of Care is adequate and (b) whether it is being carried out.
The Nurse Supervisor records in the clinical record the date, who was contacted, the questions asked and the responses, and signs and dates the entry.

If the response shows the plan is not adequate, the Nurse Supervisor arranges immediate reassessment by a licensed person under CLN-03 and CLN-04. If the plan is not being carried out properly, the Nurse Supervisor takes corrective action immediately. Corrective action may include re-instruction of the CHHA, a competency check, or reassignment. The action is documented and the Director of Nursing/HCSS is told the same day.

At least once in every 60-day period, the Nurse Supervisor visits the client in the home. The visit is sooner when a trigger event occurs. After a hospitalization or facility stay, the visit is made before or at the first visit after return to home service.

During the in-person re-evaluation, the Nurse Supervisor reviews the Plan of Care with the client. The review covers diagnoses and problems; vital signs (temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure) and a pain assessment; functional status; psycho-social status; nutrition and diet; home safety including fall risk; and the emergency plan.

If the Plan of Care is changed, the Nurse Supervisor documents the reasons by reference to the review items above. The plan is revised, signed with the licensed person's designation and dated, per CLN-04.
The Nurse Supervisor reviews the revised Plan of Care with the CHHA and documents that review. Any new task is delegated and competency is checked under CLN-05 and CLN-06.
Where a CHHA is present at the visit, the Nurse Supervisor observes the CHHA's skills and documents the observation under CLN-09.
The Nurse Supervisor documents any communication with the patient, family, significant other or designated party about complaints or problems. A complaint is also logged under ADM-09.
The Nurse Supervisor signs and dates the re-evaluation record within [NUMBER] business days of the visit. The record names any employees present, their licensure status and the skills observed.
The original and any revised Plan of Care are kept in the client's record, and copies of revised plans are given to the patient or representative within [NUMBER] business days.

If a review cannot be completed on time (for example, the client is unavailable), the Nurse Supervisor documents each attempt and notifies the Director of Nursing/HCSS. The review is completed as soon as possible, and the late review is reported to Quality Assurance under ADM-14.
The Director of Nursing/HCSS audits timeliness and completeness of 30-day contacts and 60-day re-evaluations monthly and reports results to the Administrator.

responsibilities.duty: Completes and documents 30-day contacts and 60-day in-person re-evaluations, revises the Plan of Care when needed, takes corrective action and signs and dates all entries.
Monitors due dates, reassigns overdue reviews, audits compliance and reports results.
