Participates in the review of the Plan of Care, reports changes in condition and follows revised instructions.
Ensures adequate nursing staff to meet review timelines and reviews audit results.
Files re-evaluations and revised plans and sends copies of revised plans to the patient or representative.

documentation: 30-day contact note (date, person contacted, whether plan is adequate and being carried out, responses, signature)
60-day in-person re-evaluation record with the review of vital signs, pain, function, psycho-social, nutrition, home safety/fall risk and emergency plan
Reasons for any Plan of Care change
Names, licensure status and skills observed for employees present; confirmation of plan review with the CHHA
Record of communication with patient/family about complaints or problems
Original and revised Plans of Care and proof copies were given to the patient or representative
Due-date tracking report and audit results

policies.title: Nurse Supervisor Observation of CHHA Clinical Performance
policies.applies_to: Nurse Supervisors, the Director of Nursing/HCSS and all CHHAs employed by [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To make sure that when a Nurse Supervisor directly observes a CHHA's skills, the observation is evaluated and recorded in the CHHA's employee file in a consistent form.
policies.policy:
Whenever the Nurse Supervisor directly observes a CHHA's skills, [AGENCY NAME] documents the observation in the CHHA's employee file. This policy meets Best Practices §II, Documentation Requirement Relating to the Clinical Performance of the CHHA, items 1 through 6 (II/CHHA Clinical Performance Documentation 1-6). The employee file reflects: (1) the skills directly observed; (2) an evaluation of how well those skills were performed; (3) any demonstrations or instructions provided by the Nurse Supervisor, if applicable; (4) the date of the observation; (5) the signature of the employee being evaluated; and (6) the signature of the Nurse Supervisor.

Under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7, the supervisor must ensure the CHHA demonstrates competence in each delegated task. For Medicaid PCA clients, the RN directly supervises the PCA in the home, with additional visits for a new PCA, nurse delegation or changed needs (N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.5). Direct observation under this policy is one way these duties are carried out. Observation is also done at the 60-day in-person re-evaluation when the CHHA is present (CLN-08).

definitions.definition: The Nurse Supervisor watches the CHHA perform one or more delegated tasks or skills in the client's home or in a skills-check setting.
The form kept in the CHHA's employee file listing the skills observed, the evaluation, any instruction given, the date and the signatures.
Teaching the Nurse Supervisor gives during or after the observation, such as showing the correct technique or re-explaining a task.

procedures: The Nurse Supervisor plans observations. They are done during each 60-day in-person re-evaluation when a CHHA is present, during Medicaid PCA RN supervisory visits, for each new CHHA assignment, and when a new delegated task is added or a performance concern arises.
Before the visit, the Nurse Supervisor reviews the Plan of Care and the tasks delegated to the CHHA, and chooses the skills to be observed.

During the visit, the Nurse Supervisor tells the client and the CHHA that an observation is being done. The Nurse Supervisor then watches the CHHA perform the selected skills, with attention to client safety, infection control, client dignity and following the Plan of Care.
The Nurse Supervisor completes the observation record, listing each skill directly observed.

For each skill, the Nurse Supervisor records an evaluation of how well it was performed (for example, performed correctly, needs improvement, or not competent) and short comments describing what was seen.

If a skill was not performed correctly, the Nurse Supervisor gives a demonstration or instruction right away when this is safe. The Nurse Supervisor records what was shown or taught and how the CHHA responded.
The Nurse Supervisor stops the task and takes over if the client's safety is at risk, and notifies the Director of Nursing/HCSS the same day.
The Nurse Supervisor records the date of the observation.
The Nurse Supervisor reviews the completed record with the CHHA. The CHHA signs the record. If the CHHA disagrees, the CHHA may write a comment on the form and still signs to acknowledge receipt.
The Nurse Supervisor signs the record, which is delivered to the office within [NUMBER] business days to be filed in the CHHA's personnel record.

Where an observation shows a CHHA is not competent in a delegated task, the Nurse Supervisor removes the task from the CHHA's assignment until competency is shown. The Nurse Supervisor arranges re-instruction and a repeat observation within [NUMBER] days and records the outcome. The client's Plan of Care and coverage are adjusted so the client's needs are still met.

A serious or repeated performance problem is reported to the Director of Nursing/HCSS and the Administrator. They decide on further action under PER-09 and PER-13, including reporting required under SAF-01 and ADM-06.
The Nurse Supervisor notes in the client's clinical record that an observation took place, without placing evaluation details that belong in the employee file.
The Director of Nursing/HCSS reviews observation records quarterly to identify training needs and reports trends to Quality Assurance (ADM-14).

responsibilities.duty: Observes CHHA skills, evaluates performance, gives instruction, completes and signs the observation record and follows up on deficiencies.
Performs tasks as delegated during the observation, accepts instruction, and signs the record.
Ensures observations are completed, reviews records and follows up on serious or repeated problems.
Files the signed observation record in the employee file.

documentation: Observation record in the employee file with: skills observed; evaluation of performance; demonstration/instruction given; date; CHHA signature; Nurse Supervisor signature
Follow-up re-instruction and repeat observation record
Note in the client's clinical record that an observation occurred
Quarterly summary of observation findings

policies.title: Scope of Services: What Caregivers May and May Not Do
policies.applies_to: All CHHAs, Nurse Supervisors, schedulers, intake staff and clients/representatives of [AGENCY NAME], for private-pay and Medicaid (PCA, MLTSS, Personal Preference Program) services.
policies.purpose: To define the tasks a CHHA may perform, to keep services within the written Plan of Care and delegation, and to describe the Medicaid PCA service limits and the agency's rules on private work and live-in situations.
policies.policy:
CHHAs employed by [AGENCY NAME] perform only the tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor and listed on the client's Plan of Care (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(c)). The supervisor ensures that the CHHA demonstrates competence in each delegated task and documents every delegated task in the client's record (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(d)-(e)). A CHHA may not perform a task that is not on the Plan of Care, that has not been delegated or that the CHHA has not been shown competent to perform.

For Medicaid PCA clients, the agency follows the limits in N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.8. PCA is not authorized for respite, stand-alone supervision, companionship, child care, parenting tasks, mental-health service needs, non-functional diagnoses, acute short-term conditions or needs that are not hands-on only. There is no PCA reimbursement if the PCA lives in the beneficiary's home. PCA services are not reimbursed in the settings the rule lists, including assisted living, nursing facilities, hospitals and adult day health. PCA services provided by a family member are not covered except under the Personal Preference Program. The agency does not bill PCA for services outside these limits, and it does not provide such services under a Medicaid authorization.

Private-pay services are also limited to the Plan of Care and the signed service agreement (ADM-12). CHHAs may not work privately for agency clients outside the agency. Any services arranged directly between a CHHA and a client are outside the agency and are prohibited. Pay, overtime and recordkeeping for CHHAs as domestic service employees follow 29 CFR Part 552 (see PER-12).

definitions.definition: A task the health care practitioner supervisor (an RN) has assigned to a CHHA after determining the CHHA is competent, documented in the client's record.
Presence in the home without hands-on personal care tasks. It is not an authorized Medicaid PCA service.
Any paid work a CHHA does for an agency client or the client's family outside the agency, which this policy prohibits.
The written plan that lists the tasks and hours for the client, prepared and signed by an appropriately licensed person.

procedures: At intake and at the in-person nursing assessment, the Nurse Supervisor discusses with the client or representative what services CHHAs may and may not provide. The discussion is documented.
The licensed person who prepares the Plan of Care lists each task, its frequency and its hours. Tasks that are not delegable or not covered by the payer are not placed on the plan.
The Nurse Supervisor delegates tasks to the CHHA, confirms competence in each task (CLN-05, CLN-06) and documents each delegated task in the client's record.
Before the first visit, the scheduler gives the CHHA the Plan of Care task list. The CHHA reads it and asks the Nurse Supervisor about anything unclear.
The CHHA performs only the listed tasks. If the client or family asks for a task that is not on the plan, the CHHA politely declines and tells the Nurse Supervisor the same day.
The Nurse Supervisor decides whether the request calls for a Plan of Care change, a different service, a referral or a refusal. A reassessment is done if the need is new (CLN-08).

For Medicaid PCA clients, intake staff check at intake and at each re-authorization that the request fits the PCA limits. Staff check that the setting is covered, that no relative is being paid except as permitted, and that the PCA does not live in the home. Staff coordinate with the plan or case manager under MED-01 and MED-03.

Where a Medicaid PCA client needs respite, companionship, supervision only, child care or another service PCA does not cover, intake staff tell the client, document the need and refer to the care manager or other appropriate resource. The agency does not provide the service under the Medicaid authorization.

Where two or more Medicaid clients share a residence, the scheduler and Nurse Supervisor split hours between individual hands-on tasks and shared household tasks according to the authorization (MED-01).

The CHHA reports to the Nurse Supervisor any request to take on private work, any offer of payment outside the agency and any situation where the CHHA is asked to live in the client's home. The Nurse Supervisor notifies the Administrator.

If a CHHA is found working privately for an agency client, the Administrator investigates, documents the findings and applies discipline under PER-13, up to termination. Any billing affected is reviewed and corrected under ADM-06.

The Nurse Supervisor reviews actual tasks performed (weekly activity sheets, CLN-07) against the Plan of Care at each 30-day contact and 60-day re-evaluation. Any task performed outside the plan is addressed with the CHHA right away and documented.
Staff are trained on this policy at orientation (PER-06) and at annual in-service (PER-07). Each CHHA signs an acknowledgment of the scope rules.

responsibilities.duty: Performs only delegated tasks on the Plan of Care, declines other requests, reports requests to the Nurse Supervisor and does not work privately for agency clients.
Writes or reviews the task list, delegates and documents tasks, confirms competence and responds to scope questions.
Screens requests against payer limits, assigns CHHAs to the Plan of Care and gives clients accurate information.
Investigates scope violations and private-work reports and ensures billing matches covered services.

documentation: Plan of Care with task list
Documentation of each delegated task and competence check in the client's record
Notes of discussions with clients about service limits and declined requests
Referral notes for needs outside scope
CHHA signed acknowledgment of scope rules
Investigation records for any scope or private-work violation

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
policies.applies_to: CHHAs, Nurse Supervisors and intake staff of [AGENCY NAME] for all clients.
policies.purpose: To set limits on CHHA involvement with medications, so that medication-related tasks are performed only when delegated and documented by the RN and so that medication problems are quickly reported.
policies.policy:
A CHHA works under the supervision of a New Jersey registered nurse and follows a delegated nursing regimen or performs delegated tasks consistent with the Board of Nursing's nurse delegation rules at N.J.A.C. 13:37-6.2 (N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2, as quoted in the Board's Training Book). Under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7, a CHHA may perform only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor. The supervisor ensures the CHHA demonstrates competence in each delegated task and documents each delegated task in the client's record.

At [AGENCY NAME], any medication-related task a CHHA performs is limited to what the RN has delegated and documented. If a task is not delegated, the CHHA does not perform it. The CHHA never changes, skips, adds or adjusts a medication dose or schedule. The CHHA records medication problems and reports them to the Nurse Supervisor right away. The client's medication list is part of the intake interview and the in-person nursing assessment (CLN-01, CLN-03) and is reviewed at each re-evaluation (CLN-08).

Where the client is able to take his or her own medicines, the CHHA supports the client's own self-administration in the ways the RN has authorized in writing. The RN decides which tasks are delegable and to whom, and makes that decision case by case.

definitions.definition: The client takes his or her own medication. The client makes the decisions and does the act of taking it, with any support the RN has authorized.
A medication-related task the RN has assigned to a CHHA under the nurse delegation rules, after confirming competence, and documented in the client's record.
Any concern such as a missed dose, refused dose, suspected wrong medication, apparent side effect, unclear or missing label, running low on supply or a medication change the CHHA was not told about.
The current list of the client's prescription and non-prescription medicines and supplements, obtained at intake and updated at assessments.

procedures: At intake, the intake staff member asks the client or representative for a list of all medications, including prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements, and who manages them. The list is recorded as part of the intake interview (CLN-02).
At the in-person nursing assessment, the RN reviews the medication list with the client against the medicine containers, notes allergies, and assesses the client's ability to take medications safely.

The RN decides whether any medication-related task will be delegated. If so, the RN documents the specific task, the client, the CHHA assigned and how the task is to be done on the Plan of Care and in the client's record.
If the RN decides a task will not be delegated, the Plan of Care states that the CHHA performs no medication task. The RN explains this to the client and family and documents the discussion.
Before the CHHA performs any delegated medication task, the RN confirms the CHHA is competent to perform it and documents the competency (CLN-05, CLN-06).

The CHHA reads the Plan of Care before each assignment and performs only the medication tasks delegated for that client. The CHHA does not perform a medication task for another client based on instructions for this client.
The CHHA never changes a dose, time or route, never gives extra or missed doses, never takes medicine from one container to another and never gives a medicine that is not on the delegated list.
If a client asks the CHHA to do a medication task that has not been delegated, the CHHA declines politely, explains that the nurse must approve it and contacts the Nurse Supervisor.

The CHHA reports any medication problem to the Nurse Supervisor immediately by phone or through the on-call line (ADM-11). The CHHA does not wait for the end of the visit if there is a risk to the client.
In an emergency, such as a suspected overdose, a severe reaction or a client who is unresponsive, the CHHA calls 911 first and then notifies the Nurse Supervisor (CLN-13).

The CHHA records the medication problem and the report on the weekly activity sheet (CLN-07). The Nurse Supervisor documents the report, instructions and follow-up in the clinical record the same day.

The Nurse Supervisor contacts the client's prescriber or pharmacy, or tells the client or family to do so, as appropriate. The Nurse Supervisor updates the medication list and Plan of Care if medications change.
At each 30-day contact and 60-day in-person re-evaluation, the Nurse Supervisor reviews the medication list, reviews any problems reported and confirms delegations remain appropriate (CLN-08).
Medication errors and near-misses are reported through the incident reporting process (SAF-02). The Nurse Supervisor reviews the cause and retrains staff if needed.
The Director of Nursing/HCSS reviews medication-related incidents and problem reports quarterly and reports trends to Quality Assurance (ADM-14).

responsibilities.duty: Reviews the medication list, decides what, if anything, is delegated, confirms competence, documents delegation and follows up on reported problems.
Performs only delegated medication tasks, never changes doses or schedules, and reports and records medication problems immediately.
Obtains the medication list at intake and gives it to the RN.
Oversees compliance, reviews incidents and ensures staff training.

documentation: Medication list in intake record and nursing assessment
RN delegation documentation for each medication task, including competence
Plan of Care statement on medication tasks (delegated or none)
Weekly activity sheet entries for medication problems
Nurse Supervisor notes on reports, prescriber/pharmacy contact and follow-up
Incident reports for medication errors

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits, Continuity of Care, EVV and Timekeeping
policies.applies_to: Schedulers, CHHAs, Nurse Supervisors, billing and payroll staff of [AGENCY NAME], for all clients. EVV requirements apply to Medicaid personal care services delivered in the home.
policies.purpose: To make sure visits are scheduled and delivered as planned, missed visits are handled promptly and safely, clients receive continuous care from qualified CHHAs, and visit and time records are accurate for clients, payers and payroll.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] schedules visits to match each client's Plan of Care and authorization, and it tracks every visit. Electronic visit verification (EVV) is required for Medicaid personal care and home health services delivered in the home under Section 12006(a) of the 21st Century Cures Act (42 USC 1396b(l)). New Jersey's EVV aggregator is HHAeXchange. All Medicaid personal care visits are recorded through EVV in the manner required by the payer.

Medicaid PCA services are billed under code T1019 in 15-minute units. The New Jersey fee-for-service PCA rate is $26.68 per hour (NJ SPA 24-0013, effective July 1, 2024). Managed care organization rates are contracted and are not set by this policy. Billing is based on documented units of service actually delivered.

When a visit is missed, the agency notifies the client and the Nurse Supervisor and arranges coverage with a CHHA who has had the pre-start competency review in that home (CLN-06). Weekly activity sheets (CLN-07) are separate from EVV and are still required for every client. EVV does not replace them. CHHA time is recorded accurately for payroll, and overtime and recordkeeping are handled under federal domestic service rules (29 CFR Part 552) and PER-12.

definitions.definition: An electronic system that records, at the time of service, the type of service, the client, the caregiver, the date and the start and end times of the visit. It is used for Medicaid personal care services delivered in the home.
The EVV aggregator used by New Jersey for Medicaid personal care visits.
The billing code for Medicaid personal care services, billed in 15-minute units.
A scheduled visit that does not take place, or a visit that is substantially shorter than scheduled, for any reason, including CHHA absence, client unavailability or refusal.
The review that confirms a CHHA is competent in the tasks needed in a client's home before services start there (CLN-06).

procedures: At intake, the scheduler gets the Plan of Care task list, the authorized or agreed hours, the days and times the client needs care and any special needs. The scheduler matches a CHHA with the competence the Plan of Care requires and who has had the pre-start competency review in that home (CLN-06, ADM-08).
The scheduler gives the client the visit schedule and the agency's phone number for changes and, for after-hours, the on-call number (ADM-11).
The scheduler assigns one primary CHHA and one or more named backup CHHAs when possible, to promote continuity of care. The Nurse Supervisor is informed of changes in the assigned CHHA.

For Medicaid personal care clients, the scheduler sets up the client and the CHHA in the EVV system before the first visit. The CHHA is trained on how to clock in and out. Visits are scheduled within the authorization, using T1019 15-minute units.

At each Medicaid visit, the CHHA records the start and end of the visit through EVV at the client's home as trained. If EVV cannot be completed (for example, a system or phone failure), the CHHA calls the office right away so the visit can be recorded using the payer-approved manual or exception method. The reason is documented.

For all clients, the CHHA also completes the weekly activity sheet (CLN-07). Office staff compare the sheet with EVV and schedule records weekly. Differences are resolved with the CHHA and documented.

The scheduler checks daily for visits not started, using the EVV system or the schedule. If a CHHA has not started a visit within [NUMBER] minutes of the scheduled time, the scheduler calls the CHHA and the client.

If a CHHA cannot make a visit, the CHHA calls the office as early as possible and at least [NUMBER] hours before the visit, except in an emergency. The CHHA does not arrange substitutes on his or her own.

If the client cancels or is not at home, the CHHA waits as directed by the scheduler, then calls the office. The scheduler documents the reason and tells the Nurse Supervisor if the client's safety or condition is a concern. A client who cannot be found or reached is handled under CLN-13.

When a visit is missed for any reason, the scheduler tells the client or representative and the Nurse Supervisor the same day. The scheduler arranges coverage by a CHHA who has had the pre-start competency review for that home, as soon as possible.

If no qualified CHHA is available, the Nurse Supervisor assesses the risk to the client with the client or representative, documents it and arranges an alternative, such as a family caregiver, a care manager contact or an earlier or later visit. A client at high risk is escalated to the Director of Nursing/HCSS.
The scheduler documents each missed visit: date, client, scheduled CHHA, reason, who was notified and when, and the coverage arranged or the reason none was possible.
Medicaid clients' care manager or plan is informed of missed visits as the payer requires (MED-03). Missed visits are never billed.

Billing staff bill Medicaid personal care only from verified EVV and documented visit data, in 15-minute units under T1019, and only for services delivered within the authorization. Billing discrepancies are corrected before submission.

Payroll staff pay CHHAs for time worked based on accurate time records, following federal domestic service rules (29 CFR Part 552) and PER-12. CHHAs may not record time they did not work and may not clock in or out for another person.

The Administrator reviews monthly the numbers of missed visits, late starts, EVV exceptions and continuity measures (number of different CHHAs per client). The results are reported to Quality Assurance (ADM-14) with corrective action.

responsibilities.duty: Matches CHHAs to clients, sets up EVV, monitors visit starts, arranges coverage for missed visits, notifies clients and Nurse Supervisors and documents.
Arrives on time, records the visit through EVV, completes weekly activity sheets, gives early notice of absence and does not falsify time records.
Assesses risk from missed visits, approves coverage, confirms competence of replacement CHHAs and informs clients' payers or care managers as required.
Bills only verified services under T1019 units and pays CHHAs accurately for time worked.
Monitors missed visit, EVV and continuity measures and ensures corrective action.

documentation: Client schedule and CHHA assignments
EVV records (HHAeXchange) and exception/manual-entry records with reasons
Weekly activity sheets
Missed-visit log: date, reason, notifications, coverage arranged
Nurse Supervisor risk assessments for uncovered visits
Billing records tied to verified visits (T1019, 15-minute units)
CHHA time records and payroll records
Monthly missed-visit and EVV exception reports

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
policies.applies_to: All Certified Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CHHAs), Nurse Supervisors, on-call clinicians and scheduling staff serving private-pay, NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS and Personal Preference Program clients
policies.purpose: To make sure any change in a client's condition, any emergency in the home, and any failure to carry out the plan of care is recognized, reported, assessed by a licensed person and corrected immediately, and that clients get emergency care without delay.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires every CHHA to report promptly to the Nurse Supervisor the status changes listed in the client's plan of care. Each plan of care names the specific changes the CHHA must report for that client. CHHAs follow the emergency plan recorded at the in-person assessment and call 911 for any emergency. CHHAs do not diagnose, treat or wait for a callback before calling 911. If the Nurse Supervisor learns that the plan needs revision, a licensed person reassesses it immediately (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(e)). If the plan is not being carried out properly, the agency takes corrective action immediately (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(f)). The agency keeps the original and each revised plan and gives copies to the client or representative (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(h)). Placements continue to match the level of care in the current plan (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(b)). A CHHA performs only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor, and the supervisor documents each delegated task in the client's record (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(c), (e)). A change in condition never authorizes a CHHA to perform a task that has not been delegated.

definitions.definition: Any new or worsening physical, cognitive, emotional or functional status, or any change in the home environment or caregiver situation, that is listed in the plan of care as reportable or that a reasonable person would see as affecting the client's health or safety.

A situation that may threaten life, limb or safety, such as unresponsiveness, chest pain, difficulty breathing, stroke signs, serious bleeding, a fall with suspected injury, choking, fire, or violence.
The New Jersey registered nurse who supervises the CHHA and the program of care delivered (N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2) and who acts as the health care practitioner supervisor under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7.

A person licensed in New Jersey who is appropriately qualified to evaluate the client's needs and write or revise the plan of care, and who signs it with his or her license designation (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(a)).

procedures: At the in-person assessment (CLN-03), the assessing nurse lists in the plan of care the status changes the CHHA must report for this client (for example, new confusion, falls, skin changes, refusal of care, changes in eating or breathing, or a change in the caregiver situation) and records the client's emergency plan: emergency contacts, physician, preferred hospital, and medical alerts.

The Nurse Supervisor reviews the reportable changes and emergency plan with the CHHA at the competency check before services start in the home (CLN-06) and documents the review. A copy of the emergency plan is kept in the home where the CHHA can find it.
In an emergency, the CHHA calls 911 first, gives first aid or CPR only within training and the emergency plan, and stays with the client until emergency responders arrive and take over.

After calling 911, the CHHA notifies the Nurse Supervisor or the on-call clinician (ADM-11) at [PHONE] as soon as it is safe to do so, and then notifies the client's emergency contact or representative listed in the plan.

For a non-emergency change in condition listed in the plan, the CHHA notifies the Nurse Supervisor or on-call clinician immediately by phone. The CHHA does not rely on text messages or on the weekly activity record for reporting.
The CHHA writes down what was observed, the time, and whom he or she notified. This goes on the weekly CHHA activity record (CLN-07) and in a note for the Nurse Supervisor.

The Nurse Supervisor or on-call clinician takes the report, asks about symptoms and safety, and tells the CHHA what to do within the CHHA's delegated tasks. If there is any doubt about safety, the Nurse Supervisor directs the CHHA to call 911 or arranges for medical evaluation.

The Nurse Supervisor documents the report in the client's record the same day. The entry shows the date and time, who reported, the change, instructions given, who was notified (client, representative, physician or practitioner, MCO care manager, county ADRC or Personal Preference Program consultant, as applicable), and the outcome.

If the change suggests the plan of care may be inadequate, the Nurse Supervisor arranges for a licensed person to reassess the plan immediately. The reassessment is not deferred to the next 30-day contact or 60-day visit (CLN-08).

When the plan is revised, the licensed person signs it with his or her license designation. The Nurse Supervisor documents any newly delegated tasks and verifies that the CHHA demonstrates competence in each before the CHHA performs it (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(d), (e)).

If the revised plan changes the level of care needed, the Administrator or scheduling staff confirm the assigned worker's certification matches the new level (ADM-08) and reassign if needed. The agency gives the original and the revised plan to the client or representative and keeps both in the record (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(h)).

If the Nurse Supervisor finds, from a CHHA report, a client or family complaint, a missed task, or a supervisory observation, that the plan is not being carried out properly, the Nurse Supervisor takes corrective action immediately. Examples are retraining the CHHA, redelegating or reassigning, adding supervision or correcting scheduling. The Nurse Supervisor records the finding, the action and the follow-up date.

For clients receiving Medicaid services, the Nurse Supervisor also notifies the MCO care manager (MLTSS), PCA case manager or Personal Preference Program consultant of a significant change, hospitalization or need for a changed authorization, as required in MED-03.

The CHHA or Nurse Supervisor completes an incident report (SAF-02) the same day for any emergency response, injury, fall, hospitalization or unplanned event. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is handled under SAF-01.
The Nurse Supervisor reviews all emergencies and corrective-action cases at least quarterly with the Administrator as part of quality assurance (ADM-14) to identify trends.

responsibilities.duty: Follows the emergency plan, calls 911 in emergencies, reports listed status changes immediately, documents what was observed and does not perform undelegated tasks.

Lists reportable changes in the plan, takes reports, directs the response, arranges immediate reassessment when the plan needs revision, takes immediate corrective action, delegates and documents new tasks and notifies others as required.
Reassesses the plan immediately when asked, revises it, and signs it with his or her license designation.
Is reachable at all times services are provided and handles the Nurse Supervisor's duties under this policy after hours (ADM-11).
Makes sure reassignment, scheduling, incident review and quality assurance follow-up occur.

documentation: Plan of care showing reportable changes and the emergency plan
Nurse Supervisor's note of each reported change or emergency, with notifications and outcome
Revised plan of care, signed with license designation, and proof copies were given to the client or representative
Record of tasks newly delegated and the CHHA's demonstrated competence
Corrective-action entries with dates and follow-up
Incident report (SAF-02) and weekly CHHA activity record (CLN-07)

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Nurse Supervisors, scheduling and billing staff, and CHHAs, for all private-pay, NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS and Personal Preference Program clients
policies.purpose: To ensure services end in a planned, documented and safe way. Each client receives written notice and help finding other providers so that no client is left without needed care because of how the agency discontinues services.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] plans for discharge from the start. The plan of care carries discharge goals, written by the licensed person who prepares the plan (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(a)). The agency discontinues services only for a documented reason and gives the client or representative written notice of discontinuation with a referral to other providers or, for Medicaid clients, to the MCO care manager or county Area Agency on Aging – Aging and Disability Resource Connection (ADRC). The agency does not abandon a client. For Medicaid clients, the agency follows the NJ Medicaid PCA provider-transfer rules and the instructions of the MCO or the Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services (DMAHS), and it supports the person-centered service planning requirements applicable to home and community-based services under 42 CFR 441.301(c). Client records are retained under REC-01. Until the effective date of discontinuation, the agency continues to carry out the plan of care and to match placements to the level of care in the plan (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(b), (f)).

definitions.definition: Measurable outcomes in the plan of care that describe when services are no longer needed or may change, such as regained independence, a stable caregiver arrangement or transition to a different level of care.
Ending of agency services for any reason, whether initiated by the client, the agency, a funding source or by events such as hospitalization or death.
Movement of a client's services to another provider agency, program or setting, including a change of PCA provider under NJ FamilyCare.

The client's NJ FamilyCare managed care organization (MLTSS care manager) and the county Area Agency on Aging – Aging and Disability Resource Connection, which screen and assist adults 21+ seeking MLTSS.

procedures: When the plan of care is written (CLN-04), the licensed person includes discharge goals and any anticipated transition. These are reviewed at each 30-day contact and 60-day in-person evaluation (CLN-08) and updated when the plan is revised.

The Nurse Supervisor identifies possible reasons for discontinuation early. Examples are goals met, client or representative request, move, admission to hospital or facility, death, loss of payer authorization, non-payment, need for a level of care the agency cannot provide, or a threat to the safety of the client or staff.

For any agency-initiated discontinuation, the Administrator and Nurse Supervisor review the case together, document the reason and the steps already tried to resolve it, and the Administrator approves the decision in writing before notice is given.

The agency gives the client or representative written notice of discontinuation at least 14 calendar days before the last day of service. It also explains the reason in plain language and offers to discuss it. A shorter notice is allowed only when the client requests it, or when immediate safety of the client or staff requires it. The reason for any shorter notice is documented.

With the notice, the agency gives a written referral to other providers. For private-pay clients, this includes at least [NUMBER OF REFERRAL OPTIONS] other licensed HCSFs or agencies when available. For Medicaid clients, the agency refers them to the MCO care manager, the county ADRC or the Personal Preference Program consultant, as applicable.

For Medicaid clients, the Nurse Supervisor or Administrator notifies the MCO care manager, PCA case manager or consultant on the day notice is given and cooperates in finding a replacement provider. The agency follows the PCA provider-transfer rules and does not end services in a way that conflicts with the authorization or the MCO's transfer instructions.

The Nurse Supervisor coordinates the handoff with the receiving provider, with the client's written consent where required (ADM-10). The agency sends a copy of the current plan of care, current delegated tasks, emergency plan and a summary of the client's status and needs.
Scheduling staff keep the client's schedule in place until the effective date. Missed visits are handled under CLN-12 so that care continues during the notice period.

If the client is hospitalized or admitted to a facility, the Nurse Supervisor documents the date and determines with the client or representative whether services will resume. If services will not resume, the notice and referral steps above apply, as soon as the agency learns of the decision.
If the client dies, the Nurse Supervisor records the date, closes the record, notifies billing staff, and arranges the return of any client property under CR-03.

On or before the last day of service, a Nurse Supervisor completes a discharge summary. It lists the reason for discharge, status at discharge, goals met or unmet, the referral and handoff given, and when and how written notice was provided.
The agency returns all client keys, belongings and documents, collects any agency equipment, and confirms final billing under ADM-12 with no charges after the discharge date.
The client or representative receives a copy of the final plan of care. The discharge notice, referral, summary and proof of delivery are filed in the client record.
If a client or representative disagrees with the discontinuation, the Administrator explains the grievance process under ADM-09 and, for Medicaid clients, the right to contact the MCO or DMAHS.
The Administrator closes the record and retains it in accordance with REC-01. Discharges are reviewed quarterly in quality assurance (ADM-14) to look for patterns.

responsibilities.duty: Includes discharge goals in the plan of care and signs it with license designation.
Monitors for discharge triggers, coordinates handoff, writes the discharge summary and keeps the plan current until discharge.
Approves agency-initiated discontinuations, issues written notice and referrals, communicates with MCOs and ADRC, and closes and retains the record.
Maintain service through the notice period, stop services and billing on the effective date and return client property.
Continues delegated tasks through the last visit and reports any concerns about the transition to the Nurse Supervisor.

documentation: Plan of care with discharge goals and revisions
Administrator's written approval of agency-initiated discontinuation, with reason
Written notice of discontinuation and proof of delivery
Written referral list or MCO/ADRC referral record
Transfer packet and consent to release information
Discharge summary signed by the Nurse Supervisor
Final billing statement and property return receipt

policies.title: Employment Application and Applicant Interview
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Nurse Supervisors and any staff who receive applications or interview applicants for employment involving health care services
policies.purpose: To ensure that every person [AGENCY NAME] considers for health care employment completes a full written application and is interviewed, and that the agency can confirm identity, credentials, work history, training and background before placement.
policies.policy: Every applicant for employment involving health care services completes a written application before hire. The application collects: (1) the applicant's name, including any nicknames, address, telephone number and e-mail address if available (Best Practices §III, Employment Application 1); (2) New Jersey license or certificate number, the type of license, the licensing authority and the expiration date (Employment Application 2); (3) date of birth (Employment Application 3); (4) Social Security number (Employment Application 4); (5) names, addresses and telephone numbers of all employers during at least the preceding year, including supervisors' names, dates of employment, work experience and reasons for leaving (Employment Application 5(a)-(d)); (6) education and training, including training dates and locations, degrees or certificates, CPR training, and dates of issue and expiration (Employment Application 6); (7) the applicant's date and signature (Employment Application 7); and (8) authorization to conduct a criminal background check (Employment Application 8). Every applicant is interviewed, and the agency documents the interview, including the interviewer's name and title and the interview date (Best Practices §III, Interview Documentation). The agency places and refers only actively certified HHAs it employs (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(a), (b)). Because the Board of Nursing will not certify an initial HHA applicant until it finds no disqualifying criminal history in FBI or NJ State Police files (N.J.S.A. 45:11-24.3 et seq.), the agency treats the background check authorization as a required part of every application and does not hire an applicant who refuses to sign it. Application and interview practices comply with Title VII of the Civil Rights Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act.

definitions.definition: Any person who applies for a position that involves providing or supervising health care services for the agency.
The agency's standard employment application form, completed and signed by the applicant, containing every element listed in this policy.
A signed record of the interview showing at least the interviewer's name and title and the date of the interview.

procedures: The Administrator maintains one standard Employment Application form that includes a field for every element in Best Practices §III, Employment Application 1 through 8. Before use, the Administrator reviews the form against this policy and keeps the master copy on file.

Front-office staff give the application to every person seeking health care employment, in print or electronically, before any interview. No one is hired, scheduled or placed without a completed application.
The application asks for full legal name, any nicknames or other names used, home address, telephone number and e-mail address if the applicant has one (Employment Application 1).

The application asks for the applicant's New Jersey license or certificate number, the type (for example, CHHA or RN), the licensing authority (for example, the NJ Board of Nursing) and the expiration date (Employment Application 2).

The application asks for date of birth and Social Security number (Employment Application 3 and 4). The application is stored in the confidential personnel file, and Social Security numbers are never placed on schedules, name tags, e-mails or client records.

The application has space for all employers during at least the year before the application. For each, the applicant lists the name, address and telephone number, supervisor's name, dates of employment, work experience and reason for leaving (Employment Application 5(a)-(d)). If the applicant was not employed, the applicant says so and explains how the time was spent.

The application records education and training: dates, location, any degree or certificate, CPR training, and dates of issue and expiration (Employment Application 6). This includes the CHHA training program and its completion date.

The applicant signs and dates the application (Employment Application 7). A reviewer returns any application that is unsigned, undated or missing required fields for completion before it is processed.

The applicant signs a separate authorization to conduct a criminal background check (Employment Application 8). The Administrator starts the check under PER-10. An applicant who refuses to authorize it is not considered further.

The Administrator or Nurse Supervisor reviews the completed application within [NUMBER] business days and checks it for completeness and consistency. Gaps or conflicts in dates, license numbers or training are resolved before the interview ends or before any offer.

Every applicant is interviewed by the Administrator, the Nurse Supervisor or a designee before an offer is made. Interviews cover job-related qualifications, certification, experience, availability, and knowledge of the CHHA role and scope of services (CLN-10).

Interview questions are limited to job-related topics, consistent with Title VII. Interviewers do not ask about race, religion, national origin, sex, pregnancy, age, marital or family status or genetic information. Under the ADA, interviewers do not ask about disability or medical conditions. They may ask whether the applicant can perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation. Health screening is handled after a conditional offer under PER-05.
The interviewer completes and signs an Interview Record that shows the interviewer's printed name and title, the date of the interview, and a brief summary (Interview Documentation).

The Administrator files the application, the signed background check authorization and the Interview Record in the applicant's personnel file (PER-04). Records of applicants who are not hired are kept separately and secured.

Before any referral or placement, the Administrator verifies the applicant's certification under PER-03, completes reference checks under PER-02 and confirms background checks under PER-10. The agency places only actively certified CHHAs that it employs.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the application form, ensures every required element is collected, keeps application records secure, and confirms that no one is placed before the application and interview are complete.
Interviews clinical applicants as needed, assesses clinical qualifications, and signs the Interview Record.
Provide and collect applications, check for completeness and forward to the Administrator.
Completes the application accurately, signs and dates it and authorizes the criminal background check.

documentation: Signed and dated Employment Application with all elements of Best Practices §III, Employment Application 1-8
Signed criminal background check authorization
Interview Record with interviewer name and title and interview date
Copy of the master application form and review dates

policies.title: Reference Checks
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Nurse Supervisors and staff who obtain or review references for applicants for employment involving health care services
policies.purpose: To obtain and document appropriate references for every applicant so the agency can confirm work history, conduct and suitability before placing a CHHA in a client's home.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] obtains written and/or appropriately documented verbal references from at least two individuals for every applicant, before placement (Best Practices §III, References). At least one reference must be (1) an employer, including an immediate past employer, or (2) an educator, including an instructor from a CHHA training program, if applicable. References do not include family members or friends. The applicant's file documents, for each reference: (1) the name of the person giving the reference and that person's relationship to the applicant; (2) the dates of the applicant's employment; (3) the content of the reference, including the reasons for leaving employment; (4) for written references, the signature and title of the reference and the date signed; and (5) for verbal references, the signature of the agency staff member who obtained the reference and the date of the call (Best Practices §III, References Documentation 1-5). Pre-written letters of recommendation are acceptable if verified by the agency. The agency places only actively certified CHHAs it employs, so reference checking supplements, and does not replace, credential verification under PER-03 (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(a), (b)).

definitions.definition: A reference completed and signed by the referent on the agency's reference form or other document, showing the referent's title and the date signed.
A reference obtained by telephone or in person and recorded by an agency staff member on the agency's Reference Check Form, who signs it and dates the call.
A letter prepared by the referent in advance, usually given to the applicant. It is accepted only after the agency verifies it directly with the author.
Anyone related to the applicant by blood, marriage or domestic partnership, or a personal friend. These people may not serve as references.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a Reference Check Form with fields for every element in Best Practices §III, References Documentation 1-5. The form is part of the hiring packet.

At application (PER-01), the applicant lists at least three potential references with name, telephone number, employer or school and relationship. The agency asks for more than two so that at least two usable references result.
The reviewer screens the list. Family members and friends are rejected, and the applicant is asked for a replacement.

The Administrator confirms that the final set includes at least one employer (the immediate past employer where the applicant has one) or at least one educator, such as the CHHA training program instructor. If the applicant has been out of work, a former employer or a CHHA program instructor is used.

The staff member contacts each reference by telephone or sends the written reference form within [NUMBER] business days after the application is received. Each attempt, successful or not, is recorded with the date.

For a verbal reference, the staff member asks the referent's name and relationship to the applicant, the dates the applicant worked or studied there, the applicant's work performance, reliability, and care of clients or patients, whether the person would rehire, and the reason the applicant left. The staff member writes the answers on the Reference Check Form.
The staff member then signs the Reference Check Form and writes the date of the call (Best Practices §III, References Documentation 5).

For a written reference, the staff member checks that the referent's name, relationship to the applicant, dates of employment, content including reasons for leaving, the referent's signature and title and the date signed are all present (Documentation 1-4). Incomplete forms are returned to the referent for completion, or the agency completes the reference by telephone instead.

If an applicant brings a pre-written letter of recommendation, the staff member calls or writes to the author to confirm that the author wrote and signed it, and records the verification as a verbal reference with the staff member's signature and date. An unverified letter is not counted toward the two required references.

The Administrator reviews every reference for concerns such as an unfavorable reason for leaving, concerns about client safety or reliability, or abuse, neglect or theft. Any concern is discussed with the applicant and documented. Unresolved concerns are resolved before hire.
No CHHA is referred, placed or scheduled until at least two acceptable references are in the file and the Administrator initials and dates the reference review.
All references are filed in the personnel record (PER-04). Referents' statements are kept confidential and are not shared with the applicant except as required by law.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures two acceptable references, including one employer or educator, are on file and reviewed before any placement.
Contacts referents, completes and signs the Reference Check Form with the call date, and verifies pre-written letters.
Provides contact details for appropriate references and does not list family members or friends.

documentation: Reference Check Form for each verbal reference, signed by the staff member and dated
Written references showing the referent's signature, title and date
Verification record for any pre-written letter of recommendation
Log of contact attempts
Administrator's initialed and dated reference review

policies.title: Verification of Credentials and Annual Licensure Check
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Nurse Supervisors and all CHHAs and licensed clinicians employed by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every individual the agency places holds a current NJ license, registration or certificate, and that the agency keeps proof of the original verification and of annual re-verification.
policies.policy: Before referral or placement of any licensed, certified or registered individual, and after personal examination of the original or other reliable verification source, [AGENCY NAME] keeps a copy of the employee's current license, registration or certificate, together with a copy of the Division of Consumer Affairs online verification printout confirming current status (Best Practices §III, Verification of Credentials). The agency also verifies licensure status each year using the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs online verification page, and the printout is filed in the personnel record. The agency establishes the yearly verification date as January 15 (or the next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday) (Best Practices §III, Personnel Record 8). The agency may refer or place only actively certified HHAs it employs (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(b)). Under N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2, a CHHA works under the supervision of a New Jersey registered nurse, so the agency also verifies the RN license of each Nurse Supervisor on the same schedule. No individual is scheduled for client care while certification or licensure is expired, suspended, revoked or not verified.

definitions.term: Original or other reliable verification source
definitions.definition: The original certificate or license document inspected in person, or another source the agency considers reliable, such as the issuing board's online verification.
A dated printout or PDF from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs online license verification page that shows the individual's name, credential type, number, status and expiration date.
A CHHA whose NJ Board of Nursing certificate is current and in good standing on the date of verification. Certificates renew every two years.
The date each year, set by the agency, on which all staff credentials are re-verified: January 15.

procedures: During the interview process (PER-01), the Administrator asks the applicant to bring the original certificate or license. The applicant is told that no referral or placement can occur until this is verified.

The Administrator personally inspects the original document and compares the name with a government-issued photo ID. The Administrator records the credential number, type, issuing authority and expiration date.
The Administrator makes a legible copy of the certificate or license and signs and dates the copy with the notation "original seen."

On the same day, the Administrator checks the status on the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs online verification page. The Administrator prints or saves a printout showing the verification date, current status and expiration date. If the page cannot be accessed, the Administrator contacts the NJ Board of Nursing Call Center at 973-504-6430 (Mon-Fri, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.) and documents the call in the file until a printout can be obtained.

If the status is anything other than active (for example expired, lapsed, suspended, revoked, or restricted), or if the information does not match the original, the individual is not placed and the Administrator documents the discrepancy and the action taken.

The Administrator files the copy of the credential and the verification printout in the personnel record (PER-04) before the individual's name appears on any client schedule. Only actively certified CHHAs are assigned.

The Administrator maintains a Credential Tracking Log listing each employee's credential type and number, expiration date, date of last verification and date of next annual verification. The log is reviewed monthly.

Each year on January 15 (or the next business day), the Administrator re-verifies every employee's status on the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs online verification page. The printout is dated and filed in the personnel record as the annual verification (Best Practices §III, Personnel Record 8).
The Administrator verifies the RN licenses of each Nurse Supervisor and other licensed clinicians on the same annual schedule.

Ninety days before a credential expires, the Administrator reminds the employee in writing to renew (PER-11). The Administrator verifies the renewed credential on the online page within [NUMBER] business days after the expiration date and files a new printout and copy.

If an employee's credential lapses or is suspended, revoked or restricted, the Administrator removes the employee from client assignments immediately. The Administrator notifies the Nurse Supervisor so affected clients are reassigned, and records the action. The employee may return to care only after a new verification showing active status.
The Administrator reports verification results quarterly in the quality assurance review (ADM-14), including any lapses discovered and corrective steps.

responsibilities.duty: Examines originals, obtains printouts, performs the annual January 15 verification, maintains the Credential Tracking Log and removes uncertified staff from placement.
Does not assign clinical work to anyone not verified, and tells the Administrator of any concerns about credentials.
Provides the original credential, renews on time and immediately informs the agency of any change in status.

documentation: Copy of current license, registration or certificate, marked "original seen," dated and signed
Initial Division of Consumer Affairs online verification printout
Annual verification printouts dated on or about January 15
Credential Tracking Log
Notes on any discrepancies, lapses and corrective actions

policies.title: Personnel Record Contents
policies.applies_to: Administrator and all staff who create, file or access personnel records for CHHAs, Nurse Supervisors and other employees
policies.purpose: To make sure each employee has a complete, organized and confidential personnel record that shows qualifications, competence, supervision and training, and that supports accurate identification of the person caring for a client.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel record for every employee involved in health care services. In addition to the application and credential documents required by PER-01 and PER-03, each record contains: clinical competency documentation (Best Practices §III, Personnel Record 2); performance evaluations (Personnel Record 3); clinical supervision documentation (Personnel Record 4); in-service attendance records (Personnel Record 5); the malpractice insurance policy number, if applicable to the individual (Personnel Record 6); the date of hire (Personnel Record 7); and a photograph of the employee, with the face clearly visible like those required for a passport, matching the photograph used for the employee's identification badge (Personnel Record 9). The annual verification of licensure status required by Personnel Record 8 is kept in the same file under PER-03. The clinical competency documentation includes the supervisor's record of the CHHA's demonstrated competence in each delegated task (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(d), (e)). The photograph on file must match the ID tag worn at all times while giving care, which shows first name or initial, full surname, certification or licensure level and photograph (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.7(a)). Personnel records are kept separate from client records and are confidential. Employee medical and exposure records, including those required by the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard (29 CFR 1910.1030), are kept in a separate confidential medical file.

definitions.definition: The employee's file kept by the agency, in paper or secured electronic form, that holds the items listed in this policy and in PER-01, PER-02, PER-03, PER-05 and PER-10.
Signed records showing that the Nurse Supervisor or other qualified evaluator observed and found the employee competent in the tasks the employee may perform (PER-08, PER-09, CLN-06).
Records of the Nurse Supervisor's supervision of the CHHA, including on-site observations and delegation records (CLN-05, CLN-09).
A recent photograph of the employee's face, clearly visible and unobstructed, like those required for a passport.

procedures: On the date of hire, the Administrator opens a personnel record using a standard Personnel Record Checklist that lists every required item, including Best Practices §III, Personnel Record 2 through 9.
The Administrator records the date of hire on the record cover sheet and on the checklist (Personnel Record 7). A hire date is entered before the employee is scheduled for any shift.

The Administrator takes a photograph of the employee on the first day, against a plain background, face clearly visible and not covered by hats, sunglasses or masks. It is filed in the record (Personnel Record 9).

The agency uses the same photograph to make the employee's ID badge. The badge shows first name or initial, full surname, certification or licensure level and the photograph, with letters of equal size and at least 1/4 inch high. The badge is at least as large as any other ID worn (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.7(a); see ADM-13). The Administrator checks that the badge photo matches the file photo before issuing the badge.
If the employee's appearance changes significantly or the photograph is more than [NUMBER] years old, the Administrator takes a new photograph and reissues the badge and file photo together.

The Nurse Supervisor files clinical competency documentation (Personnel Record 2): initial competency testing (PER-08), the competency check before services begin in each new client home (CLN-06), and ongoing assessments (PER-09). Each task record shows the evaluator's name and credential, the date and the result.
The Nurse Supervisor files performance evaluations (Personnel Record 3) after the initial period of employment and at least annually, signed and dated by the evaluator and the employee.
The Nurse Supervisor files clinical supervision documentation (Personnel Record 4): on-site observations (CLN-09), delegation and supervision notes, and corrective-action or coaching documents.
The Administrator files in-service attendance records (Personnel Record 5), showing the topic, date, hours, presenter and employee signature (PER-07).

If the employee is covered by an individual malpractice or professional liability policy, the Administrator files the policy number and carrier (Personnel Record 6). If none applies, the Administrator notes "not applicable" and the reason on the checklist.

Application, interview, reference, credential, annual verification, health attestation and background check records are filed in the same personnel record under PER-01, PER-02, PER-03, PER-05 and PER-10, so a surveyor can find every required item in one place.

Employee medical, TB-screening and bloodborne pathogen exposure or vaccination records are kept in a separate, locked or access-controlled confidential medical file, not in the general personnel record, consistent with 29 CFR 1910.1030.

Personnel records are stored in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator, the Nurse Supervisor and designated staff may view them. Personnel files are never stored with, and never mixed into, client records (REC-01).

Each quarter, the Administrator audits a sample of at least [NUMBER] personnel records against the checklist, corrects deficiencies within [NUMBER] business days and reports the results in the quality assurance review (ADM-14).
When an employee leaves, the Administrator records the separation date and keeps the record for the period required by the agency's retention schedule and applicable law.

responsibilities.duty: Opens and maintains the personnel record, records date of hire, takes the photograph, issues matching ID badges, files in-service and insurance information, secures records and audits them.
Completes and files competency documentation, performance evaluations and clinical supervision records on time.
Provides accurate information, attends in-service training, signs required records and tells the agency of any change affecting the record, including insurance or appearance.

Date of hire entry
Passport-style photograph matching the ID badge
Clinical competency records
Performance evaluations
Clinical supervision records
In-service attendance records
Malpractice policy number, if applicable
Separate confidential employee medical file
Quarterly record audit results

policies.title: Employee Health Attestation and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All Certified Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CHHAs) and any other employee who may have direct client contact, and the staff who maintain personnel records.
policies.purpose: To make sure that no CHHA is placed in a client's home until the agency has a signed health attestation on file. The attestation documents the results of a Mantoux tuberculin skin test and proof of immunity to rubella and rubeola. This protects clients and staff and supports the agency's duty to place only qualified, agency-employed aides under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires every CHHA to complete a Health Attestation Form before the first client assignment. This policy meets Best Practices §III, Personnel Record 1 (Health attestation form, reflecting the results of Mantoux tuberculin skin test as well as rubella and rubeola immunization or serologic evidence of immunity). The form must show (a) the Mantoux tuberculin skin test result and (b) rubella and rubeola immunization, or serologic (titer) evidence of immunity. The completed form is filed in the employee's personnel record before the first assignment. The agency will not schedule an employee for client care until the form is in the record and has been reviewed by the Director of Nursing (DON). Only agency-employed CHHAs may be placed (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(b)), so this requirement applies to each aide on the agency payroll. The agency handles health information as confidential employee medical information and handles any occupational exposure in line with the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030).

definitions.definition: The agency form completed and signed by the employee and by a licensed health care practitioner (or documented by the practitioner's records). It reports TB screening and immunity results.
A skin test for TB infection. The result is recorded as millimeters of induration, with the dates placed and read and the interpretation.
A laboratory titer report showing immunity to rubella or rubeola (measles).

procedures: The Human Resources (HR) designee gives each conditional hire the Health Attestation Form with the offer letter and explains that it must be complete before the first assignment.

The employee arranges the Mantoux TST with a licensed practitioner, clinic or the agency's occupational health provider. The employee is told that a TST requires two visits, to place and to read the test, so it should be started early.
The practitioner records the TST date placed, date read, millimeters of induration and interpretation on the form, or attaches the laboratory or clinic report.

If the employee has a documented prior positive TST, the employee provides that documentation and the practitioner's written evaluation (for example, symptom screen and/or chest radiograph result) in place of a new skin test. The DON reviews it.
For rubella and rubeola, the employee provides either an immunization record or a laboratory titer showing immunity. The form is not complete without both.

If the employee has no proof of immunity, the HR designee refers the employee to a practitioner for vaccination or a titer. The employee is not scheduled for client care until proof is received, unless the DON documents a practitioner-directed plan that the DON accepts.
The employee signs and dates the attestation, and the practitioner signs where the form requires it.
The HR designee checks the form for completeness (TST result, rubella evidence, rubeola evidence, signatures, dates) and sends it to the DON for clinical review.
The DON documents any abnormal finding, a positive TST or any condition that may affect client safety. The DON arranges follow-up and decides whether the employee may be assigned.
The HR designee files the completed, reviewed form in the personnel record before the first assignment and enters the completion date in the scheduling system's clearance checklist.
The scheduler may not assign an employee whose checklist shows the health attestation as incomplete.

The DON sets repeat TB screening intervals and post-exposure follow-up in the agency's TB and exposure-control procedures (see SAF-03). HR tracks each due date and notifies the employee 30 days before it.

Under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030, the agency offers hepatitis B vaccination to employees with occupational exposure at no cost. Acceptance or declination is documented. Exposure incidents are handled under the agency's Exposure Control Plan.

Employees must report any symptoms of active TB or a diagnosed communicable disease to the DON immediately. The DON removes the employee from client contact until a practitioner clears the employee in writing.
During annual file audits, the HR designee confirms that every employee file has a completed attestation and reports gaps to the Administrator within five business days.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures that no employee is assigned without a completed attestation and supports corrective action when gaps are found.
Reviews every attestation, decides on clinical follow-up for abnormal results, and authorizes clearance for assignment.
Distributes, tracks and files forms, and maintains the due-date tracking.
Confirms clearance status before making any assignment.
Obtains testing, gives accurate information, signs the form and reports symptoms or exposures promptly.

documentation: Signed Health Attestation Form with Mantoux TST result and rubella and rubeola immunity evidence, filed in the personnel record before the first assignment
Supporting laboratory, clinic or immunization records
DON review note and any follow-up or clearance letters
Hepatitis B vaccine acceptance or declination form
Clearance checklist showing completion date
TB re-screening due-date tracking log

policies.title: Agency Orientation
policies.applies_to: All newly hired CHHAs, the DON and Nurse Supervisors who deliver or approve orientation, and the HR designee who keeps attendance records.
policies.purpose: To prepare each new CHHA to work safely, ethically and within the delegated scope of care for [AGENCY NAME] clients, and to document that preparation in a form the Division of Consumer Affairs can review.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] provides an orientation program quarterly to all newly hired CHHAs. Each CHHA completes orientation within three months of the date of hire, or sooner based on the CHHA's documented level of expertise. This policy meets Best Practices §III, Agency Orientation (orientation offered quarterly, within three months of employment or sooner based on documented expertise).

Orientation covers at minimum the following 13 topics, which satisfy Best Practices §III, Agency Orientation topics 1-13: (1) infection control; (2) blood-borne pathogens; (3) child abuse; (4) elder abuse; (5) domestic violence; (6) pain management; (7) patient rights; (8) HIPAA; (9) corporate compliance; (10) ethical considerations in home care delivery, including receipt of gifts and money from clients and other financial transactions; (11) employee safety; (12) emergency procedures; and (13) agency administrative and clinical policies and procedures.

Orientation documentation satisfies Best Practices §III, Agency Orientation documentation 1-4: (1) an outline of topics covered; (2) the length of time for each mandatory topic; (3) the date and signature of the instructor; and (4) the name, date and signature of each employee on an agency sign-in sheet. Attendance records are kept and may be electronic if readily retrievable and printable.

Orientation does not replace the clinical competency testing required before or on the first assignment (PER-08). Aides work only on tasks delegated or directed by the supervising practitioner and are placed only if actively certified and employed by the agency (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7).

definitions.definition: The agency's structured introduction of new CHHAs to the 13 required topics and to agency policies, offered at least quarterly.
Verified prior training or experience (for example, certificates or a previous employer's records) that the DON accepts in writing as meeting some or all orientation content.
A paper or electronic attendance record showing each attendee's printed name, date and signature.

procedures: The DON publishes the orientation calendar each January with at least one session per quarter and posts it for HR and the scheduler.
At hire, the HR designee tells each CHHA the date of the next session. The session must fall within three months of the hire date. If it cannot, the HR designee notifies the DON, who adds a session.

The DON may shorten or waive parts of orientation for a CHHA whose prior training or experience is documented. The DON records the basis and the topics waived in the personnel record. The shortening applies only to timing or content already verified. The CHHA still receives agency-specific policies (topic 13).

The DON prepares a written outline for each session. The outline lists the 13 mandatory topics (infection control, blood-borne pathogens, child abuse, elder abuse, domestic violence, pain management, patient rights, HIPAA, corporate compliance, ethics, employee safety, emergency procedures, and agency administrative and clinical policies and procedures).
The outline lists the minutes allotted to each mandatory topic. The instructor records the actual time spent if it differs.
The ethics topic specifically covers receiving gifts and money from clients, borrowing, handling client funds and other financial transactions. It follows CR-03 and PER-13.
The HIPAA topic covers the agency's privacy practices and the workforce training required under 45 CFR 164.530(b), and follows ADM-10.

The blood-borne pathogens and infection control topics follow 29 CFR 1910.1030 and SAF-03. The abuse, neglect and exploitation topics (child, elder and domestic violence) follow SAF-01, including the aide's duty to report.
The patient rights topic reviews CR-01. The pain management topic covers recognizing and reporting a client's pain to the nurse without giving any treatment outside the aide's delegated tasks.
The employee safety and emergency procedures topics cover SAF-04 and SAF-05 and CLN-13, including whom to call and when to call 911.
Instructors must be the DON, a Nurse Supervisor or another qualified person designated by the DON. The instructor dates and signs the outline and the attendance record.
Each attendee signs in with printed name, date and signature at the start of the session and signs at the end if the session runs more than one block.
The HR designee files the outline, the time-per-topic record, the signed sheet and the CHHA's completion note in the personnel record within five business days of the session.
If a CHHA misses a session or a topic, the DON arranges a make-up session on the missed topic within the three-month window. The make-up is documented the same way.
Electronic attendance records are kept in a system that allows retrieval and printing on request. The HR designee tests retrieval each year.
The DON reviews orientation content each year with the policy review under ADM-14 and updates it for regulatory changes.

responsibilities.duty: Schedules quarterly sessions, approves the outline, grants any documented-expertise acceleration and ensures all 13 topics are covered.
Delivers the content, tracks time per topic, and dates and signs the outline and attendance record.
Notifies new hires, collects sign-in sheets and files records.
Provides resources, audits timeliness and addresses overdue orientations.
Attends, signs in and completes make-up for any missed topic.

documentation: Written outline of topics for each session
Record of minutes spent on each mandatory topic
Instructor's date and signature
Sign-in sheet with each employee's name, date and signature
Documented-expertise determination, if used

Annual orientation calendar

policies.title: Annual Mandatory In-Service Training
policies.applies_to: All CHHAs employed by [AGENCY NAME], the DON, Nurse Supervisors and the HR designee.
policies.purpose: To keep every CHHA's knowledge of safety, infection control, abuse reporting and compliance current, and to document that each aide has completed the mandatory topics each year.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] provides an in-service program at least once each year (or over the course of a year) for all CHHAs. This policy meets Best Practices §III, Agency Mandatory In-Service 1-13. The program covers at minimum: (1) blood-borne pathogens; (2) infection control; (3) standard precautions; (4) child abuse; (5) elder abuse; (6) domestic violence; (7) pain management; (8) workforce protection; (9) employee safety issues; (10) back safety; (11) how to handle needle sticks; (12) fraud and abuse prevention; and (13) corporate compliance.

The agency may accept another HCSF's documentation that a CHHA has met some or all of these topics, and will then credit only the topics shown in that documentation.
