Attendance records are maintained. In-service training does not replace the ongoing clinical competency assessment in PER-09, and aides remain limited to tasks delegated or directed by the supervising practitioner (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(c)).

definitions.definition: Training for current employees given at least once a year, whether in one session or across several sessions during the year.
Practices that protect employees from occupational hazards, including exposure control under 29 CFR 1910.1030.
Written proof from another HCSF that the CHHA completed named in-service topics.

procedures: Each January the DON builds the annual in-service plan listing all 13 required topics, the dates or months for each and the instructor.
The plan is arranged so that each CHHA can complete all 13 topics in each 12-month period, either in one session or over several sessions (for example, quarterly modules).
The HR designee tracks each CHHA's 12-month in-service cycle from the hire date or from a fixed calendar year and notifies the CHHA and the scheduler 60 days before it ends.
Each session has a written outline with the topics, the minutes spent on each topic and the instructor's name.

Blood-borne pathogens, standard precautions, needle stick handling and workforce protection content follows 29 CFR 1910.1030 and SAF-03. Needle stick content includes immediate first aid, reporting to the DON the same day and post-exposure follow-up.
Child abuse, elder abuse and domestic violence content follows SAF-01, including the aide's duty to report and the agency's reporting steps.
Pain management content covers recognizing and reporting pain and non-drug comfort measures within the aide's delegated tasks, without assessing or treating pain outside that scope.
Employee safety and back safety content covers body mechanics, safe client handling, home hazards and workplace violence, and follows SAF-05.

Fraud and abuse prevention and corporate compliance content follow ADM-06 and include accurate time records, no billing for services not delivered, the hotline or reporting channel and non-retaliation (ADM-07).
The instructor dates and signs the outline. Each attendee signs in with printed name, date and signature. Electronic sign-in is acceptable if records are retrievable and printable.
If a CHHA offers documentation from another HCSF, the HR designee gives it to the DON. The DON verifies the employer, the dates and the topics covered, and credits only those topics in writing.
The HR designee updates each employee's training record after each session or credited transfer and files the records in the personnel record.
If a CHHA is not on track, the HR designee notifies the DON 30 days before the cycle ends. The DON arranges make-up training (live, video or other format) with documented attendance.
The scheduler does not reduce a CHHA's hours for training time that is required by this policy. Training time is paid under PER-12.
The Administrator reviews in-service completion rates each quarter and reports them to the QA committee under ADM-14.

responsibilities.duty: Builds the annual plan, approves content, verifies transfer documentation and arranges make-up.
Delivers content, records time per topic and signs the outline.
Tracks cycles, collects attendance and maintains records.
Ensures resources and follows up on non-completion.
Attends all required topics and signs in.

documentation: Annual in-service plan covering topics 1-13
Written outlines with time per topic
Sign-in sheets with name, date and signature
Instructor signature and date
Transfer documentation from another HCSF and the DON's credit note
Individual in-service tracking record in each personnel file
Make-up session records

policies.title: Clinical Competency Testing Before or at First Assignment
policies.applies_to: All CHHAs before or on their first assignment date, and the Nurse Supervisors who perform the testing.
policies.purpose: To make sure each CHHA has been tested by a nurse and has shown competence in the personal care tasks and the core knowledge areas before caring for a client, consistent with the rule that the supervising practitioner must ensure the aide demonstrates competence in each delegated task.
policies.policy:
All CHHAs undergo clinical competency testing by a Nurse Supervisor before or on the first date of assignment. A Nurse Supervisor is a New Jersey-licensed registered nurse who supervises CHHAs and the program of care (N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2). An aide may perform only tasks delegated by, or directed by, the health care practitioner supervisor, and the supervisor must ensure the aide demonstrates competence in each delegated task (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(c) and (d)).

This policy meets Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Prior to or on the date of the first Assignment, 1(a)-(h). Testing includes direct observation of delegated personal care services related to: (a) the musculo-skeletal system; (b) the integumentary system; (c) the upper and lower gastrointestinal system; (d) the urinary system; (e) the cardiovascular and respiratory systems (vital signs, antiembolic stockings, oxygen assistance, positioning); (f) the neurological system (cognitive impairment, seizure disorder, post-stroke care, rehabilitation or restorative care); (g) the endocrine system (foot care, skin care and nutrition for a client with diabetes); and (h) the promotion of sleep. If direct observation is impractical or intrusive, the Nurse Supervisor may ask the CHHA to describe how the task would be performed.

This policy also meets Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Prior to or on the date of the first Assignment, 2(a)-(g). The agency tests, by written test, oral test or direct observation, the CHHA's knowledge and communication skills in: (a) observation, reporting and documentation of patient status and care furnished; (b) basic infection control procedures; (c) basic elements of body mechanics and functioning, and changes in body function that must be reported to the Nurse Supervisor; (d) maintenance of a clean, safe and healthy environment; (e) recognizing emergencies and knowledge of emergency procedures; (f) physical, emotional and developmental needs of and ways to work with the populations served, including respect for the patient and the patient's privacy and property; and (g) adequate nutrition and fluid intake.

A CHHA who has not passed testing is not assigned to a client.

definitions.definition: A New Jersey-licensed RN designated by [AGENCY NAME] (the DON or a delegate) to test, delegate to and supervise CHHAs.
The Nurse Supervisor watches the CHHA perform a task on a person or on a skills mannequin or in a skills lab setting.
When direct observation is impractical or intrusive, the CHHA explains step by step how the task would be done.

procedures: The HR designee confirms the CHHA's credentials, health attestation and background clearance are complete (PER-03, PER-05, PER-10) and informs the DON that the aide is ready for testing.
The DON assigns a Nurse Supervisor to test the CHHA and sets the test date no later than the first assignment date. The scheduler does not assign the aide before the test is signed.
The Nurse Supervisor uses the agency's Initial Competency Checklist. The checklist lists items 1(a)-(h) and 2(a)-(g) so that each can be marked as observed, described, written or oral.
For 1(a) musculo-skeletal, the nurse observes safe transfers, positioning, body mechanics, range-of-motion only as delegated and assistance with ambulation.
For 1(b) integumentary, the nurse observes bathing, skin care, skin observation and pressure-area prevention, and checks that the CHHA reports skin changes to the nurse.
For 1(c) upper and lower gastrointestinal, the nurse observes assistance with eating, feeding, toileting, bowel care within delegated limits and reporting of changes.
For 1(d) urinary, the nurse observes toileting, incontinence care, catheter-site hygiene and emptying drainage bags only as delegated, and reporting of changes in output.
For 1(e) cardiovascular and respiratory, the nurse observes vital signs, application of antiembolic stockings, assistance with oxygen (without changing flow settings) and positioning.

For 1(f) neurological, the nurse reviews care for cognitive impairment, seizure disorders and post-stroke care, and rehabilitation or restorative care. For 1(g) endocrine, the nurse reviews foot care, skin care and nutrition for a client with diabetes. For 1(h), the nurse reviews measures that promote sleep.

If direct observation of an item is impractical or intrusive, the Nurse Supervisor asks the CHHA to describe how the task would be performed. The nurse records that the description method was used and why.

For items 2(a)-(g), the nurse uses a written test, an oral test or direct observation. The test covers documentation and reporting, infection control, body mechanics and reportable changes, a clean and safe environment, recognizing emergencies, respect for privacy and property, and nutrition and fluid intake.

The nurse sets a passing standard on each item. If the CHHA does not demonstrate competence, the nurse gives remedial instruction and retests before any assignment. A task the CHHA has not shown competence in is not delegated.
The Nurse Supervisor records the result for each item, evaluates overall competence, and signs and dates the checklist.
The nurse records in the client's record the tasks delegated to the CHHA at the first assignment (CLN-05) and, for a new home, completes the competency check under CLN-06.
The HR designee files the signed checklist in the personnel record and updates the scheduling clearance status. Ongoing assessments follow PER-09.

responsibilities.duty: Assigns the Nurse Supervisor, approves the checklist and decides when a CHHA may be assigned.
Tests the CHHA on all items, documents competence and signs the record.
Confirms pre-testing clearances and files results.
Does not assign a CHHA without a signed passing checklist.
Demonstrates the skills and knowledge; reports limits of competence.

documentation: Initial Competency Checklist covering 1(a)-(h) and 2(a)-(g), with method used for each item
Notes on any item tested by description and the reason
Written or oral test results
Remedial training and retest records
Nurse Supervisor's date and signature
Scheduling clearance record

policies.title: Ongoing Clinical Competency Assessment and Recordkeeping
policies.applies_to: All CHHAs employed by [AGENCY NAME] and the Nurse Supervisors who assess them.
policies.purpose: To make sure CHHAs remain competent in every delegated task throughout their employment, and to record that competence in the employee file in a way that can be reviewed by the state.
policies.policy:
The clinical competency of every CHHA is tested or assessed throughout the year through direct observation of skills with assigned patients and/or written or oral testing on the same skills and knowledge areas used at first assignment (PER-08, items 1 and 2). This policy meets Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Testing or assessment throughout the year. The supervisor must ensure that the aide demonstrates competence in each delegated task (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(d)).

This policy meets Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Recordkeeping 1-4. Competency documentation in the employee file includes: (1) the name of the CHHA; (2) the clinical skills tested and the date and location of testing; (3) an evaluation of the CHHA's competency; and (4) the date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor performing the testing. At minimum, an assessment of competency is recorded by the end of each year of employment. Records may be electronic.

definitions.definition: Any observation, return demonstration, written or oral test by a Nurse Supervisor that evaluates a CHHA's skills after the first assignment.
The minimum competency assessment recorded by the end of each year of employment.

procedures: The DON keeps a competency tracking list showing each CHHA's hire date, last assessment date and the date the annual assessment is due.

The Nurse Supervisor assesses each CHHA throughout the year. Common occasions include supervisory visits (CLN-09), client reviews (CLN-08), a new task being delegated, a change in a client's needs and an incident or complaint.
When a client's plan of care adds a new task, the Nurse Supervisor confirms the CHHA is competent in it and records the delegation before the aide performs it (CLN-05).

During a supervisory visit, the nurse observes the CHHA with the assigned client and compares the observed skills with the checklist items in PER-08 (musculo-skeletal, integumentary, GI, urinary, cardiovascular/respiratory, neurological, endocrine, sleep).

The nurse may also use a written or oral test on observation and reporting, infection control, body mechanics, a safe environment, emergencies, client needs, privacy and property, and nutrition and fluids.
The nurse evaluates the CHHA's competency as competent, competent with coaching or not competent for each skill tested.

If a CHHA is not competent in a skill, the nurse removes the task from the CHHA's delegation, provides instruction, and retests before it is delegated again. The nurse notifies the DON and records the follow-up.
The nurse completes a competency record that shows the CHHA's name, the skills tested, the date and location of testing, the evaluation of competency, and the nurse's signature and date.
The nurse completes the record on the day of the assessment or no later than two business days afterward, and sends it to HR.
The HR designee files the record in the personnel record, which may be in an electronic system that can be retrieved and printed.

By the end of each year of employment, the DON confirms that each CHHA has at least one assessment recorded. For CHHAs who have not been assessed, the DON schedules a nurse visit within 30 days of the anniversary.
The DON reviews the tracking list monthly and reports overdue assessments to the Administrator.
Findings that show a pattern (for example, many CHHAs not competent in one skill) are sent to the QA committee under ADM-14 and addressed in the next in-service (PER-07).
Competency records are retained as part of the personnel record under PER-04.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the tracking list, ensures annual assessments and acts on findings.
Assesses CHHAs, documents results and signs records, and adjusts delegation.
Files records and flags missing annual assessments.
Reviews compliance reports and resources.
Takes part in assessments and asks for help with any task not known.

documentation: Competency record for each assessment: CHHA name, skills tested, date and location, evaluation, Nurse Supervisor signature and date
Annual competency assessment by the end of each year of employment
Remediation and retest notes
Competency tracking list
Electronic records that are retrievable and printable

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: All applicants and employees, including CHHAs and non-certified office staff, and each officer, director, principal and owner of [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To protect clients by screening for disqualifying criminal history and by ensuring that background and registry checks are completed, documented and kept current, in line with the Board of Nursing certification process and the agency's registration obligations.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] does not place a CHHA with a client unless the CHHA holds active Board of Nursing certification. The Board will not certify an initial HHA applicant until it determines that no disqualifying criminal history record exists in FBI or New Jersey State Police files (N.J.S.A. 45:11-24.3 et seq.; N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.4). The agency treats that Board clearance as a minimum and not as a substitute for its own screening.

The agency obtains each applicant's written authorization on the application and runs its own checks for non-certified office staff and any other employee who is not subject to the Board's check. Each officer, director, principal or owner certifies criminal history at registration, and a later conviction is reported to the Division of Consumer Affairs within 30 days. All background screening is carried out in line with the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including the required disclosures, authorizations and adverse-action notices, and is handled as confidential.

definitions.definition: A criminal history record found in FBI or New Jersey State Police files that prevents Board of Nursing certification of an HHA applicant.
A background or registry report obtained from a consumer reporting agency, covered by the Fair Credit Reporting Act.
An owner, officer, director or other person with control of the agency who must certify criminal history at registration.

procedures: The employment application (PER-01) includes a separate, stand-alone disclosure and authorization for background checks, which the applicant signs before any check is run.
For CHHAs, the HR designee verifies that the Board of Nursing certification is active (PER-03). The agency does not accept a pending or lapsed certification for placement.

For CHHA applicants who are newly certified, the HR designee confirms that the Board's certification was issued after its criminal history review. The agency relies on the Board's determination that no disqualifying record exists.

For non-certified office staff and any employee not covered by the Board's check, the HR designee orders the agency's own criminal history check through a vendor and reviews the results before the person starts work.

The agency also checks the employee registries and exclusion lists the Administrator designates in the compliance program (ADM-06), such as federal and state exclusion lists for programs the agency bills. The check is done before hire and repeated on the schedule set by the Administrator.
The HR designee records the date, the source and the result of each check on a Background Check Log and files the supporting reports in a confidential section of the personnel record.

If a report contains information that may lead to a decision not to hire or to end employment, the HR designee gives the applicant or employee a copy of the report and a summary of FCRA rights before action, allows a reasonable time to respond, and then sends the final adverse-action notice if the decision stands.
The Administrator, with the DON, decides on any adverse finding, considers the position and client risk, and records the decision. No CHHA is assigned to a client while a finding is unresolved.

Employees must tell the Administrator within five business days if they are arrested for, charged with, or convicted of a crime, or if their certification is restricted. The Administrator evaluates whether the employee may continue direct care.
If the Board of Nursing suspends, revokes or does not renew a CHHA's certification, the CHHA is removed from client assignments immediately (PER-11).
The Administrator keeps a signed criminal history certification for each officer, director, principal and owner filed with the HCSF registration (ADM-02).

If an officer, director, principal or owner is convicted of a crime after registration, the Administrator reports the conviction to the Division of Consumer Affairs within 30 days and records the report (ADM-02, REC-02).
Reports are kept confidential, accessible only to HR, the Administrator and the DON, and are not placed in a client or general employee file where others may see them.
The HR designee reviews the Background Check Log each quarter to find checks that are missing or due for repeat and reports gaps to the Administrator.
The agency discards consumer reports in line with the retention policy (REC-01) and in a secure manner.

responsibilities.duty: Decides on adverse findings, files principal certifications and reports any later conviction to the Division within 30 days.
Confirms that no clinical assignment is made until clearances are complete.
Obtains authorizations, runs checks, keeps logs and issues FCRA notices.
Does not assign an employee whose clearance is incomplete.
Gives accurate information and reports arrests, charges or convictions.

documentation: Signed disclosure and authorization for background checks
Background Check Log
Criminal history and registry check reports (confidential file)
Board of Nursing certification verification (PER-03)
FCRA pre-adverse and adverse-action notices, if used
Officer, director, principal and owner criminal history certifications
Record of any conviction report to the Division of Consumer Affairs

policies.title: CHHA Qualifications, Certification and Renewal
policies.applies_to: Administrator, DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors, HR/scheduling staff and all Certified Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CHHAs)
policies.purpose: To make sure that every aide [AGENCY NAME] places in a client's home holds an active New Jersey Board of Nursing homemaker-home health aide certificate, was trained in a Board-approved program, and is removed from the schedule if the certificate lapses.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs, refers and places only actively certified New Jersey Homemaker-Home Health Aides that it employs (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7). An aide is employed by the agency and works under the supervision of a New Jersey-licensed registered nurse, who supervises both the certified aide and the program of care delivered (N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2). The aide performs only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7). Aides must have completed a Board of Nursing-approved training program of at least 76 hours, made up of 60 classroom hours and 16 clinical hours in a skills lab or patient care setting (N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.4). The Board certifies an aide only after a criminal history check clears. Certificates renew every two years. Out-of-state certifications are not valid for New Jersey in-home personal care, so an aide must hold the New Jersey certificate before any assignment. An aide whose certificate is expired, lapsed, suspended or unverified is not scheduled and does not perform client care. [AGENCY NAME] does not charge aides any fee for certification or employment (see ADM-03). The Board application fee, currently stated as $50 and nonrefundable (N.J.A.C. 13:37-5.5), is paid to the Board; the agency will confirm the current fee on the Board's pages.

definitions.definition: Certified Homemaker-Home Health Aide, certified by the New Jersey Board of Nursing and employed by [AGENCY NAME].
A current New Jersey certificate that is not expired, lapsed, suspended or revoked, confirmed by primary-source verification with the Board of Nursing.
The New Jersey-licensed RN (or physician) who delegates tasks to and supervises the aide (see ADM-01 and CLN-05).
A homemaker-home health aide training program of at least 76 hours (60 classroom, 16 clinical) approved in writing by the Board of Nursing before it started.

procedures: Before any offer of employment, HR confirms that the applicant holds a New Jersey CHHA certificate. A certificate from another state is not accepted as a substitute, and the applicant is not scheduled for client care until the New Jersey certificate is held.

HR performs primary-source verification of the certificate with the Board of Nursing before the first assignment and records the certificate number, issue date, expiration date, verification date and verifier's initials (see PER-03).

HR obtains the aide's training program name and completion documentation. The DON/HCSS confirms that the program was Board-approved and covered at least 76 hours (60 classroom, 16 clinical). If the program cannot be confirmed, the DON/HCSS asks the Board and does not place the aide until it is confirmed.
HR keeps a copy of the certificate and the training completion record in the personnel file (see PER-04).

[AGENCY NAME] does not charge applicants or aides any fee for certification, training, application or placement. Any Board fee, currently stated as $50 and nonrefundable, is paid to the Board under the Board's instructions. If the agency reimburses it, that is voluntary and documented. The Administrator confirms the current fee on the Board's pages at least annually.
HR keeps a certification expiration tracker for every aide. It records the expiration date, the renewal reminder dates and the date renewal was verified.
HR sends written reminders to the aide 90, 60 and 30 days before expiration and tells the scheduler and the DON/HCSS of any aide who has not shown proof of renewal at 30 days.
The aide submits the renewal to the Board and gives HR the renewed certificate or a Board confirmation. HR verifies it with the Board and updates the tracker within 2 business days.

If proof of active renewal is not verified by the expiration date, the scheduler removes the aide from all future shifts effective the next scheduled shift. The scheduler notifies the DON/HCSS, who arranges coverage so no client's service is interrupted (see CLN-12).
The aide may not perform any client care while lapsed. HR documents the date of removal and the date of reinstatement. Reinstatement happens only after the Board verifies the active certificate.

Aides must tell the DON/HCSS within 1 business day of any Board of Nursing action, complaint, investigation, or criminal charge or conviction. The DON/HCSS and Administrator then determine whether the aide may continue to work (see PER-10 and ADM-06).

The DON/HCSS assigns each aide only tasks delegated or directed by the supervisor, and confirms that the aide has demonstrated competence in each delegated task (see CLN-05, CLN-06 and PER-08). Certification alone does not authorize any task outside the plan of care.
Each aide is assigned to a named New Jersey-licensed RN supervisor so that the aide and the program of care are always supervised (see CLN-09).

[AGENCY NAME] does not operate a homemaker-home health aide training program unless the Administrator first obtains the Board of Nursing's written approval. If it is ever approved, the program must meet the Board's class-size and RN clinical supervision limits (no more than 30 students per instructor and no more than 10 aides per supervising RN).
The Administrator reviews the tracker monthly, with a report to the DON/HCSS, and includes certification compliance in the quality review under ADM-14.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures that only actively certified, agency-employed CHHAs are placed; reviews the expiration tracker monthly; confirms current Board fees.
Confirms training program approval; supervises and delegates tasks to aides; decides on continued work after any Board action.
Verifies certificates with the Board, maintains the tracker and sends reminders; keeps personnel file documents.
Removes any aide with a lapsed or unverified certificate from the schedule and arranges coverage with the DON/HCSS.
Maintains active certification, renews on time, provides proof to HR and reports Board actions or charges within 1 business day.

documentation: Primary-source verification record for each aide's certificate (number, dates, verifier)
Copy of the certificate and training program completion record in the personnel file
Certification expiration tracker and reminder notices
Record of removal from and return to the schedule for lapsed certificates
Supervisor assignment and delegation records
Monthly Administrator tracker review

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
policies.applies_to: Administrator, payroll and HR staff, schedulers and all hourly employees including CHHAs
policies.purpose: To make sure that [AGENCY NAME] pays all employees accurately and lawfully under federal and New Jersey wage and hour law, and registers and contributes to the State programs required of employers.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs its aides directly as employees. It does not classify aides as independent contractors. The agency pays at least the New Jersey minimum wage: in 2026 that is $15.92 per hour for most employers and $15.23 per hour for employers with fewer than 6 employees. The Administrator confirms which rate applies to the agency and documents the basis. The agency checks local ordinances in the municipalities where it operates, including Newark, Jersey City, Paterson and Trenton, and applies any more protective local requirement. The agency pays overtime and compensable travel time as required by the Fair Labor Standards Act (29 USC 201 et seq.), the Department of Labor's domestic service rules (29 CFR 552) and New Jersey wage law. Counsel confirms the agency's live-in and overnight (sleep time) pay rules before any such assignment is accepted. The agency registers with the New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development (NJDOL) and pays the unemployment, disability and family leave contributions it owes as an employer. The pay rate in client authorizations (for example, NJ FamilyCare PCA reimbursement) never reduces an aide's wage below the legal minimum.

definitions.definition: A fixed, recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods) that the agency designates in writing for overtime calculations.
Time an employee spends traveling between client homes during the workday, which counts as hours worked under federal and New Jersey law.
An assignment in which an aide stays at the client's home for an extended or overnight period; pay rules for these assignments are confirmed by counsel before the assignment is accepted.
New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development, which administers employer unemployment, disability and family leave contributions and the state minimum wage.

procedures: Before the agency hires any employee, the Administrator registers the agency with NJDOL for unemployment, temporary disability and family leave contributions, and records the employer account numbers [NJDOL ACCOUNT NUMBER] in the administrative file.

The Administrator determines whether the agency is subject to the $15.92 or $15.23 minimum wage rate for the current year, documents the number of employees used for that determination, and re-checks it on January 1 each year and whenever headcount changes.

The Administrator or HR checks the local ordinances of every municipality in which the agency has employees or clients, including Newark, Jersey City, Paterson and Trenton, each January and whenever the agency opens in a new municipality, and notes any additional requirements in a compliance memo.
HR classifies every aide as a W-2 employee at hire and sets each aide's hourly rate in writing in an offer letter. The rate may never be lower than the applicable minimum wage.
HR designates the agency's fixed workweek in writing and provides it to all employees at orientation (see PER-06).
Aides record time worked using the electronic visit verification and timekeeping system described in CLN-12. They record actual start and end times and do not round in the agency's favor.

Payroll pays all hours worked, including time at clients' homes beyond the scheduled visit, required orientation and in-service training (see PER-06 and PER-07), and compensable travel time between client visits.

Payroll calculates overtime for all hours over 40 in a workweek at one and one-half times the regular rate of pay, including all required components of the regular rate, across all clients and assignments.
Before accepting any live-in or overnight assignment, the Administrator obtains counsel's written direction on pay, sleep time, meal breaks and recordkeeping for that assignment and keeps it on file.
Schedulers do not create schedules that cause unplanned overtime without approval from the Administrator, and they do not ask any aide to work 'off the clock'.
Payroll pays all employees on a regular, published pay schedule and provides a written pay statement with each payment showing hours, rate, gross pay and deductions.

Payroll makes only deductions that the law allows or that the employee has authorized in writing. [AGENCY NAME] does not deduct charges for uniforms, ID tags, training or background checks (see ADM-03).

Employees who believe they were underpaid report it to HR or the Administrator. HR investigates within 5 business days, corrects confirmed errors on the next payroll and documents the outcome. No retaliation is allowed (see ADM-07).

Each quarter, the Administrator reviews a sample of timekeeping records against payroll to confirm accuracy, overtime and travel time compensation, and reports results to the quality review under ADM-14.
Payroll keeps payroll and time records for the period required by federal and New Jersey law, as confirmed by counsel, and makes them available to regulators on request.
The Administrator reviews this policy each January with counsel to reflect changes in minimum wage, overtime rules, local ordinances and NJDOL contribution rates.

responsibilities.duty: Registers with NJDOL; determines the applicable minimum wage; obtains counsel's guidance on live-in and overnight pay; reviews quarterly wage audits.
Classifies employees; calculates wages, overtime and travel pay; issues pay statements; keeps payroll records; investigates pay complaints.
Builds schedules that consider overtime and travel time; seeks approval before scheduling overtime.
Records time accurately and reports any pay errors.
Confirms live-in, overnight and other complex wage rules and annual updates.

documentation: NJDOL registration and account numbers
Minimum wage determination memo and annual re-check
Local ordinance compliance memo
Offer letters with hourly rates and written workweek designation
EVV and timekeeping records reconciled to payroll
Pay statements and payroll registers
Counsel's written guidance on live-in and overnight assignments
Quarterly timekeeping and wage audit results and corrections

policies.title: Staff Conduct, Professional Boundaries and Gifts
policies.applies_to: All employees, including CHHAs, Nurse Supervisors, the DON/HCSS and office staff
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of professional conduct so that clients are protected, boundaries are maintained, and employees do not use their position for personal or financial gain.
policies.policy: Employees must act ethically and keep professional boundaries with every client and family. Orientation covers ethics, including gifts, money and financial transactions with clients (see PER-06). Aides are employees of [AGENCY NAME] and work only for the agency's clients under the plan of care, performing only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7). CHHAs may not work privately for clients, meaning they may not accept private pay or arrange care for an agency client outside the agency. Employees may not borrow money or property from clients, lend money to clients, or handle client finances except as the plan of care specifically allows (see CR-03). Employees may not accept gifts beyond what this policy allows. This policy does not prevent an employee from working for another employer in general (see ADM-03).

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a caregiver's professional role from a personal, social, romantic, financial or business relationship with a client.
Anything of value given to an employee by or on behalf of a client or family, including cash, checks, gift cards, property, loans, bequests and use of a client's property.
Providing paid care or services to an agency client directly, outside of the agency, or soliciting a client to leave the agency.
Any handling of client money, cards, checks, bank accounts, or property, including borrowing, lending, purchasing and signing documents for a client.

procedures: At hire, HR gives each employee this policy and the code of conduct. The employee signs an acknowledgment that is placed in the personnel file (see PER-04).

Orientation covers ethics, professional boundaries, gifts, money and financial transactions with clients. The trainer records the date and attendance (see PER-06), and it is repeated in the annual in-service (see PER-07).
Employees may not accept cash, checks, gift cards, jewelry or other valuables, regardless of value. Employees may not be named as a beneficiary, agent, power of attorney or witness for a client.

If a client or family offers a gift, the employee politely declines, explains agency policy, and tells the Nurse Supervisor the same day. The Nurse Supervisor documents it. If refusing would seriously offend the client, the employee brings the item to the Nurse Supervisor, who decides with the Administrator what to do and documents it. Small perishable items such as a shared snack or homemade food of nominal value may be accepted.

Employees do not borrow money, property or a vehicle from a client or family, and they do not lend money or property to them. They do not sell products or services to clients or solicit donations or favors.

Employees do not handle client money, bank cards or accounts except as the written plan of care permits (for example, a documented shopping errand). When it does, the employee keeps the receipt, returns exact change, and has the client or representative sign the log (see CR-03).
Employees do not use client property, phones, vehicles or credit for personal purposes and do not take client property.

Aides do not accept private-pay work from agency clients or their families, arrange to be paid outside the agency, or refer clients to another provider. Any request must be directed to the Nurse Supervisor or Administrator.

Employees maintain professional relationships. They do not engage in romantic or sexual relationships with clients, and they do not engage with clients on personal social media or share personal contact information beyond what agency scheduling requires. They do not post any client information or images (see ADM-10).

Employees do not work under the influence of alcohol or drugs and do not use tobacco or vaping products inside a client's home. They do not discuss their personal problems, religion or politics in a way that pressures the client.
Employees do not bring friends, family or children to a client's home during work hours, and they do not accept or use a client's home for personal matters.

Any employee who learns of a boundary violation, gift, loan or suspected financial exploitation reports it to the Nurse Supervisor or Administrator immediately, and the matter is also handled under SAF-01 and SAF-02 when abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected.

The Administrator investigates reports within 3 business days, documents findings, and imposes corrective action up to and including termination. Where required, the Administrator reports to the Board of Nursing or other authorities (see ADM-06).
Employees who report violations in good faith are protected from retaliation (see ADM-07).
Nurse Supervisors review boundary and gift compliance during supervisory visits and client contacts (see CLN-08 and CLN-09), and document any concerns.

responsibilities.duty: Enforces the code of conduct; investigates reports; imposes corrective action; makes required reports.
Teach and monitor boundaries; document gift offers; check compliance during visits and calls.
Obtains acknowledgment at hire; records orientation and in-service ethics training.
Follow this policy; decline gifts; report violations and gift offers immediately.

documentation: Signed code of conduct and policy acknowledgment
Orientation and in-service ethics training attendance records
Gift offer and disposition log
Client financial transaction logs and receipts when authorized in the plan of care
Investigation notes and corrective action records
Supervisory visit notes referencing boundary compliance

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator, DON/HCSS Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Owners, governing body, Administrator, DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors and office staff
policies.purpose: To define the structure, leadership and lines of authority of [AGENCY NAME], to ensure that a qualified licensed nurse supervises clinical services, and to ensure that required ownership and management information is kept current with the Division of Consumer Affairs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is a health care service firm that places or arranges placement of personnel for health care, companion or personal care services, as defined in N.J.S.A. 34:8-45.1, and is registered with the Division of Consumer Affairs (DCA). The governing body ([GOVERNING BODY NAME]) is legally responsible for the agency's operation and appoints an Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], who manages day-to-day operations. The agency designates a New Jersey-licensed registered nurse or physician as the health care practitioner supervisor (HCSS), titled Director of Nursing (DON/HCSS), [DON/HCSS NAME], and files a copy of the supervisor's license with the DCA at registration. The DON/HCSS is responsible for all clinical services, including delegation and supervision of aides. The agency reports any change in owners or managing agents to DCA in writing within 30 days, and gives owner and managing-agent information before any change in ownership or management (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3). The roles of the DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors and office staff are documented in written job descriptions and an organizational chart.

definitions.definition: The owner(s), board or other group that holds legal responsibility for the agency and appoints the Administrator.
The person responsible for the day-to-day management of the agency, compliance and finances.
The New Jersey-licensed RN or physician who supervises clinical services and delegates tasks to aides.
A person who has authority to manage or control the operations of the agency, whose information must be provided to DCA.

procedures: The governing body adopts written bylaws or operating documents that state its authority and responsibilities. It meets at least quarterly and records minutes of its meetings.

The governing body appoints the Administrator in writing and approves the Administrator's job description, including responsibilities for compliance with DCA registration, financial and reporting requirements.

The governing body designates a New Jersey-licensed RN or physician as the HCSS/DON in writing, and HR verifies that the license is active and in good standing with the licensing board before appointment.
The Administrator files a copy of the HCSS/DON's New Jersey license with the DCA at registration, and files a replacement copy each time the license is renewed or the person changes (see ADM-02).

The DON/HCSS is responsible for: assigning and supervising Nurse Supervisors; the in-person nursing assessment and plan of care (CLN-03, CLN-04); delegation of tasks to aides (CLN-05); aide competence (PER-08, PER-09); supervision visits (CLN-08, CLN-09); and clinical on-call coverage (ADM-11).
Nurse Supervisors, who must be licensed in New Jersey, report to the DON/HCSS and perform assessments, supervision and client reviews as assigned in a written job description.
Office staff (scheduling, intake, HR and billing) perform administrative duties under the Administrator's direction. They do not perform clinical assessments, delegate tasks or give clinical advice.

The Administrator prepares and maintains an organizational chart showing reporting lines for the governing body, Administrator, DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors, office staff and aides, and updates it within 10 days of a change.

The Administrator names a qualified alternate to act when the Administrator is absent, and the governing body names a licensed alternate nurse to cover the DON/HCSS. Both alternates are documented, and the alternate's license is verified.

Before any change in ownership or management, the Administrator gives DCA the owner and managing-agent information required by N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3(b), using the DCA's online portal or the Director's forms.

The Administrator reports in writing to the Regulated Business Section of DCA any other change to application information within 30 calendar days of the change, and keeps a copy of the submission and confirmation (see ADM-02).
If an officer, director, principal or owner is convicted of a crime after filing, the Administrator obtains a new criminal-conviction affidavit and files it with DCA within 30 days of the conviction.
The Administrator reports to the governing body at each meeting on census, complaints, incidents, staffing, regulatory filings and quality results (see ADM-14).
The governing body reviews and approves this manual annually and whenever a regulation changes (see ADM-14), and records the approval in the minutes.
The Administrator keeps current copies of all job descriptions, licenses, organizational charts and appointment letters available for the DCA surveyor.

responsibilities.duty: Holds legal responsibility; appoints the Administrator and DON/HCSS; approves policies annually; oversees compliance.
Manages operations; keeps DCA information current; makes timely filings; designates alternates.
Directs all clinical services; supervises Nurse Supervisors; delegates and supervises aide tasks; keeps the license active.
Perform assessments, supervision and reviews under the DON/HCSS.
Perform administrative functions only and do not make clinical decisions.

documentation: Governing body bylaws, minutes and annual policy approval
Appointment letters for the Administrator and DON/HCSS
Copy of the DON/HCSS's NJ license filed with DCA and verification records
Job descriptions and organizational chart
Alternate designations
DCA change-reporting submissions and confirmations
Criminal-conviction affidavits and filing proof, if applicable

policies.title: HCSF Registration, Renewal, Financial Statements and Change Reporting
policies.applies_to: Owners, Administrator, finance staff and DON/HCSS
policies.purpose: To make sure that [AGENCY NAME] is, and stays, validly registered as a health care service firm with the Division of Consumer Affairs, and files on time its renewals, financial statements and change notices.
policies.policy: A firm that places or arranges placement of personnel for health care, companion or personal care services must register with the Division of Consumer Affairs (N.J.S.A. 34:8-45.1; definitions at N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.2). [AGENCY NAME] files its application through the DCA Regulated Business Licensure Portal on the Director's forms, with the firm and trade names, each primary location, officers, directors and principals, owners of 10% or more, managing agents, a criminal-conviction certification from each officer, director, principal or owner, and a list of licenses held in other states with any actions taken (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3). The registration package includes the $500 application fee, a $10,000 bond (which the Director may waive for an entity with a net worth of $100,000 or more, shown by a CPA- or licensed-accountant-certified financial report) and a certificate of general professional liability insurance of at least $1,000,000. The agency pays the annual registration fee of $500 per primary location (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-7.1, as cited from a secondary source) and confirms the current fee on the DCA portal. Under P.L. 2026, c.45, the annual expiration moves from June 30 to September 30, and registrations that already renewed for 2026-2027 are extended to September 30, 2027. The agency will confirm this with DCA because the source is secondary and DCA implementation guidance was pending. Renewal includes evidence of accreditation (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5) and the financial statements, audits and reports required by N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5A. The agency reports any change in application information in writing within 30 calendar days (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3(c)). The agency does not recruit, advertise, offer services or contract before registration is granted (see ADM-03).

definitions.definition: Health care service firm: an agency that places or arranges placement of personnel for health care, companion or personal care services and must register with DCA.
A principal place of business of the firm; the annual registration fee is charged per primary location.
A $10,000 bond securing compliance with the HCSF Act, which the Director may waive for an entity with net worth of $100,000 or more.
The DCA unit that registers and regulates HCSFs; phone (973) 504-6370, regulatedbusiness@dca.njoag.gov.
Money the firm received for NJ Medicaid personal care assistant services in the relevant year; it determines the audit or review category.

procedures: The owners and Administrator assemble the initial registration package through the DCA Regulated Business Licensure Portal (https://rgbportal.dca.njoag.gov/): firm and trade names, each primary location, officers, directors, principals, 10%-or-more owners and managing agents.
Each officer, director, principal or owner signs the criminal-conviction certification required by N.J.S.A. 34:8-44. The Administrator checks it for completeness before filing.
The Administrator lists any licenses held in other states and any actions taken against them, and includes them in the application. If none, the application states so.

The Administrator obtains the $10,000 bond or, if the agency qualifies, prepares the net-worth waiver request with a financial report certified by a CPA or licensed accountant showing net worth of at least $100,000.
The Administrator obtains a certificate of general professional liability insurance of at least $1,000,000, and uploads it with a copy of the DON/HCSS's NJ license (see ADM-01).

The Administrator pays the $500 application fee online. DCA processing reportedly averages 30 to 60 days, which is not a rule deadline. The agency does not recruit, advertise, offer services or contract until it holds the registration (see ADM-03).
The Administrator places the issued registration in the administrative file and posts the expiration date on the compliance calendar with reminders at 120, 90 and 60 days before expiration.

The Administrator confirms the current expiration date (September 30 under P.L. 2026, c.45, extended to September 30, 2027 for firms that already renewed for 2026-2027) and the current fee ($500 per primary location) with DCA or the portal before each renewal, and documents the confirmation.
The Administrator prepares the renewal in the portal and pays the annual fee for each primary location. The renewal includes evidence of current accreditation (see ADM-05).

By July 1 each year, the finance lead prepares the prior calendar year financial statement, which must match the agency's State tax filing and show assets, liabilities, gross income, operating expenses and money received for NJ Medicaid PCA services (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5A(a)), and submits it with the renewal.

The Administrator and CPA determine each year which category applies: a periodic audit if the agency received more than $250,000 in NJ Medicaid PCA revenue in the relevant year; an audit if gross income is $10 million or more; or a report including a review by a NJ-licensed CPA if PCA revenue is under $250,000 and gross income is $1 million to under $10 million. Audits must carry an unqualified opinion with compliance and financial components.

Because the audit provisions are reported as suspended, the Administrator confirms their current status with DCA in writing each year, notes the result in the file, and does not skip an audit or review unless DCA confirms it is not required. The Administrator also confirms with DCA how the July 1 financial statement date works with a September 30 expiration.

The Administrator gives DCA the owner and managing-agent information before any change in ownership or management, and reports in writing any other change to application information to the Regulated Business Section within 30 calendar days (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3(b)-(c)).
If an officer, director, principal or owner is convicted after filing, the Administrator obtains a new affidavit and files it within 30 days of the conviction (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3(d)).
The Administrator keeps all filings, receipts, confirmations and DCA correspondence for each registration year and reports status to the governing body at each meeting (see ADM-01 and ADM-14).

responsibilities.duty: Sign certifications; fund fees, bond and insurance; ensure the Administrator has resources to meet deadlines.
Files the registration, renewal and change reports; keeps the compliance calendar; confirms current fees, dates and audit status with DCA.
Prepares the financial statement, the audit or review; ensures it matches the State tax filing.
Provides current license documentation for DCA filings.

documentation: Registration application, confirmation and certificate
Criminal-conviction certifications
Bond or net-worth waiver documentation; liability insurance certificate
Fee payment receipts
Annual financial statements, audits or CPA reviews, and DCA status confirmations
Compliance calendar showing deadlines and completion
Written change reports and DCA acknowledgments

policies.title: Prohibited Acts and Advertising Limits
policies.applies_to: Owners, Administrator, HR/recruiting staff, marketing staff, schedulers and the DON/HCSS
policies.purpose: To prevent [AGENCY NAME] from committing any act that N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.6 prohibits for a health care service firm, and to keep recruiting, advertising and employment practices lawful.
policies.policy: This policy meets N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.6(a)1-4 (Prohibited acts). [AGENCY NAME] does not do any of the following. (1) It does not recruit or advertise for staff, offer services, or contract with a facility before it obtains HCSF registration. This also means it will not claim accreditation before it holds it. (2) It does not charge a fee or liquidated damages to an employee or in connection with employment, unless it also holds an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2. (3) It does not prevent an employee, by contract, from working for others, and any fee charged on that basis would also require an employment agency license. (4) It does not knowingly send employees to, or keep serving, a facility not under NLRB jurisdiction where a strike or lockout is in progress, to replace strikers. The agency's conduct rule in PER-13 that aides may not privately serve agency clients is a client-protection rule and does not bar an employee from working for another employer in general. Counsel reviews any employment agreement or policy wording that touches this subject.

definitions.definition: The agency's registration as a health care service firm issued by the Division of Consumer Affairs.
A set amount that an employee must pay the firm, for example for leaving early or for working elsewhere.
A license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2 that a firm must also hold to charge employees fees or to charge a fee for restricting their work for others.
A labor dispute in which employees stop work or an employer closes out workers, in a facility where the firm might be asked to supply replacement staff.

procedures: Before the DCA registration is issued, the Administrator confirms in writing to owners, recruiting and marketing staff that recruiting, advertising, offering services and contracting with any facility are not permitted.

The Administrator keeps the date of registration in the administrative file. Job postings, websites, social media, brochures, business cards, signs and referral-source outreach are not published or distributed until that date.

Marketing materials are approved in writing by the Administrator before use. The approval checks that statements are accurate, include the agency's registration status only when held, and do not state or imply accreditation, Medicaid or MCO participation, or licensure that the agency does not currently hold.

The agency does not claim accreditation in advertising until the accreditation body has granted it. After that, the Administrator verifies the claim is current (see ADM-05) and removes it within 1 business day if accreditation is lost.

HR does not charge any applicant or employee a fee of any kind in connection with employment, including application, placement, training, background check, certification, ID tag, uniform, orientation or testing fees, and does not collect deposits for them.
The agency's employment agreements, offer letters and handbook do not contain liquidated damages, training repayment, or placement fee terms. Counsel reviews each template and each change before use.
The agency does not hold the aide's pay or deduct from wages for any such charges (see PER-12).

The agency does not include any contract term that prohibits an employee from working for another employer. If the agency wants to charge a fee on that basis, it will first obtain an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2, which requires the governing body's written approval.

Before accepting any contract with a hospital, nursing home or other facility, the Administrator asks whether a strike or lockout is in progress and whether the facility is under NLRB jurisdiction, and documents the answer.

The agency does not knowingly send any employee to, or keep serving, a facility not under NLRB jurisdiction where a strike or lockout is in progress, to replace strikers. If the Administrator learns that such a dispute exists, the agency stops placements, notifies the DON/HCSS and counsel, and does not resume until counsel clears it in writing.
No employee is required to accept an assignment that would replace striking workers. Employees who raise a concern are protected from retaliation (see ADM-07).
The Administrator reviews the agency's job ads, website, social media and marketing materials every quarter against this policy and records the review.

Employees who learn of a possible violation report it to the Administrator or Compliance Officer immediately. The Administrator investigates within 5 business days, corrects the practice, refunds any improper fee to the employee, and reports as required under ADM-06.
The Administrator trains recruiting, marketing and scheduling staff on this policy at hire and annually, and keeps signed acknowledgments.

responsibilities.duty: Approves any decision to seek an employment agency license; makes sure the agency does not operate before registration.
Approves all marketing and employment forms; checks facility strike or lockout status; investigates and corrects violations.
Does not collect employee fees or use restrictive terms; does not post jobs before registration.
Obtain approval of all materials; do not claim registration or accreditation not held.
Do not assign staff to facilities during a strike or lockout without clearance.
Reviews employment forms and strike or lockout questions.

documentation: Registration date record and pre-registration hold notice
Marketing and advertising approval log and quarterly review records
Reviewed employment application, offer letter and agreement templates with counsel sign-off
Facility strike or lockout inquiry records
Employee acknowledgments of this policy
Violation reports, investigations, corrections and refunds

policies.title: Placement of Aides: HCSF Licensure and Agency-Employed CHHAs Only
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Director of Nursing/Health Care Practitioner Supervisor, scheduling and intake staff, human resources, and all Certified Homemaker-Home Health Aides (CHHAs) placed by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] places certified homemaker-home health aides only while it holds a current Health Care Service Firm (HCSF) registration, and only with aides who are its own employees and hold an active New Jersey certificate.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(a) and N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(b).

N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(a): To place certified homemaker-home health aides, [AGENCY NAME] is licensed as a health care service firm by the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. The agency will not refer or place any aide into a client's home unless its HCSF registration is current. If the registration lapses, is suspended or is revoked, no new placements are made until the Administrator confirms with the Division of Consumer Affairs that placement may resume. The Administrator will notify the Division, and clients, as required by ADM-02 and ADM-05.

N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7(b): [AGENCY NAME] refers or places only actively certified homemaker-home health aides who are employed by the agency. The agency does not use independent contractors, registry-style referrals of aides it does not employ, or aides supplied by another firm to fill CHHA assignments. An aide whose certificate is expired, inactive, suspended or revoked, or who holds only an out-of-state certificate, will not be placed.

Certificate status is verified before the first shift and again at least annually (see PER-03 and PER-11). Aides perform only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor (see CLN-05).

definitions.definition: A business registered with the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, Regulated Business Section, that places health care personnel, including certified homemaker-home health aides, with patients.
An aide holding an active certificate issued by the NJ Board of Nursing.
Assigning, referring or sending an aide to provide services in a client's home.
On [AGENCY NAME]'s payroll as an employee with required tax withholding, not engaged as an independent contractor.
A certificate that is current, not expired, suspended, revoked or otherwise restricted, as confirmed against Board of Nursing records.

procedures: The Administrator keeps the current HCSF registration certificate on file at [ADDRESS] and confirms before each renewal cycle that it remains in effect (see ADM-02).

The Administrator immediately stops all new aide placements if the HCSF registration lapses, is suspended or is revoked. The Administrator documents the date and reason in the compliance file and notifies the Director of Nursing and scheduling staff the same day.
Human resources hires every CHHA as a W-2 employee. No CHHA is engaged as an independent contractor, through a staffing intermediary, or on a 1099 basis.

Before extending an offer, human resources collects a copy of the applicant's NJ Board of Nursing CHHA certificate and verifies it against Board of Nursing records (see PER-03). Verification is printed or saved and dated.

Out-of-state certificates, expired certificates, and certificates that are not active are not accepted. The applicant is told in writing that placement cannot occur until an active NJ certificate is shown.
Human resources records certificate number, issue date, expiration date and verification date in the personnel record (see PER-04) and in the credential tracking log.
Scheduling staff may assign an aide only if the credential tracking log shows 'Active – verified' with a verification date before the first shift.
Human resources re-verifies each aide's certificate at least once every 12 months, and again before a known certificate expiration date. Results are signed and dated in the personnel record.

Human resources sends reminders to each aide 90, 60 and 30 days before certificate expiration. An aide whose certificate expires is removed from the schedule on the day of expiration until renewal is verified (see PER-11).

If scheduling staff cannot cover a shift with an agency-employed, active CHHA, they notify the Director of Nursing/Health Care Practitioner Supervisor, who offers the client rescheduling or another employed CHHA. Staff will not call an outside aide, an independent contractor or another firm's aide to cover (see CLN-12).
Before any placement, the Director of Nursing/Health Care Practitioner Supervisor confirms that the aide's tasks are delegated and recorded in the plan of care (see CLN-04 and CLN-05).

The Administrator reviews the credential tracking log quarterly and compares the active-aide roster with payroll to confirm every placed aide is an employee. Discrepancies are corrected within 5 business days and documented.

If an aide is found to have been placed with an inactive certificate, the Administrator removes the aide from the schedule at once, notifies the Director of Nursing, completes an incident report (SAF-02), reviews affected visits with the Director of Nursing, and reports as required under ADM-06 and REC-02.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the HCSF registration, halts placements if registration is not in good standing, and reviews the credential and payroll reconciliation quarterly.

responsibilities.role: Director of Nursing/Health Care Practitioner Supervisor
responsibilities.duty: Ensures only active, agency-employed CHHAs are assigned, and that delegated tasks are documented.
Hires CHHAs as employees, verifies certificates before the first shift and annually, and maintains the credential tracking log.
Assign only aides shown as 'Active – verified' and never use outside or contract aides.
Keep certification current, report any change in certificate status immediately, and renew on time.

documentation: HCSF registration certificate and renewal records
Board of Nursing certificate verification (dated) for each CHHA
Credential tracking log with certificate number, expiration and verification dates
Annual re-verification records in each personnel file
Quarterly active-aide/payroll reconciliation
Incident reports and corrective actions for any placement error

policies.title: Accreditation Maintenance and Loss Reporting
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Director of Nursing/Health Care Practitioner Supervisor, compliance officer, quality assurance staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] obtains accreditation from a New Jersey Department of Human Services-recognized accrediting body within 12 months of registration, keeps it in force, shows evidence of it at each registration renewal, and reports any loss of accreditation to the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs within 10 days.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will obtain accreditation from an accrediting body recognized by the NJ Department of Human Services within 12 months of its HCSF registration (P.L. 2014, c.29; P.L. 2018, c.48). The agency will keep that accreditation continuously in effect for as long as it is registered as an HCSF.

Evidence of accreditation is required with each annual registration renewal under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5, and [AGENCY NAME] will include current evidence with every renewal filing. If accreditation is lost, withdrawn, suspended, expired or not renewed, the Administrator will report it in writing to the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, Regulated Business Section, within 10 days.

The agency will not advertise itself as accredited unless the accreditation is current (see ADM-03).

definitions.definition: An organization recognized by the NJ Department of Human Services to accredit health care service firms.
The current accreditation certificate or letter from the accrediting body showing the agency's name, accreditation status and effective dates.
Any denial, withdrawal, revocation, suspension, lapse or non-renewal of accreditation, whether or not the agency disputes it.
The annual renewal of the HCSF registration with the Division of Consumer Affairs.

procedures: At registration, the Administrator records the date of registration and calendars the 12-month accreditation deadline. The Administrator sets internal checkpoints at 3, 6 and 9 months.

Within 60 days after registration, the Administrator confirms with the NJ Department of Human Services or the Division of Consumer Affairs the current list of recognized accrediting bodies, and selects one in writing. The selection and date are recorded in the compliance file.
The Administrator submits the accreditation application, with the fee, no later than month 3 after registration and files the confirmation.

The Administrator assigns the compliance officer to maintain an accreditation readiness file, with current policies, personnel records, training records, quality assurance reports and client records, and holds a mock survey before the accreditor's visit.
The Director of Nursing/Health Care Practitioner Supervisor corrects any deficiency identified in a mock survey within 14 days and documents the correction.
During the accreditor's survey, the Administrator is the primary contact. The Administrator keeps a copy of the survey findings.
The Administrator submits any plan of correction to the accrediting body by the deadline given and tracks it to closure.

Within 5 business days of receiving the accreditation decision, the Administrator files the certificate or letter in the compliance file and enters the effective and expiration dates in the compliance calendar.
The compliance officer calendars the accreditation renewal date and begins renewal preparation at least 6 months before expiration.

At least 90 days before registration renewal, the Administrator confirms that accreditation is current and prepares a copy to submit as evidence of accreditation with the renewal filing (see ADM-02). The Administrator confirms with the Division what other documents the renewal requires.

If the agency receives any notice that accreditation may be denied, suspended, withdrawn or not renewed, the Administrator informs the governing body within 2 business days and starts a written response plan.

If accreditation is lost, the Administrator sends a written report to the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, Regulated Business Section (regulatedbusiness@dca.njoag.gov; (973) 504-6370; or through the NJ Regulated Business Licensure Portal) within 10 days of the loss. A copy of the accreditor's notice is attached. The Administrator keeps proof of submission.
When accreditation is lost, the Administrator immediately removes all references to accreditation from the website, brochures and client materials, and informs staff.
The Administrator submits a corrective action plan to the governing body within 10 days and meets with the accrediting body to seek reinstatement, with the date and outcome documented.
The quality assurance committee reviews accreditation status at every quarterly meeting (see ADM-14).

responsibilities.duty: Selects the accrediting body, meets the 12-month deadline, submits evidence at renewal, and reports any loss to the Division of Consumer Affairs within 10 days.
Maintains the accreditation readiness file and compliance calendar, and conducts mock surveys.

responsibilities.role: Director of Nursing/Health Care Practitioner Supervisor
responsibilities.duty: Ensures clinical records and practices meet accreditation standards and corrects clinical deficiencies.
Receives accreditation status reports and approves corrective action plans.

documentation: Accreditation application, fee receipt and correspondence
Accreditation certificate/letter and survey findings
Plans of correction and closure records
Compliance calendar showing 12-month deadline, accreditation expiration and renewal date
Copy of evidence of accreditation submitted with each registration renewal
Written report to the Division of Consumer Affairs, with proof of submission, if accreditation is lost
Quality assurance meeting minutes noting accreditation status

policies.title: Corporate Compliance Program, Misconduct Response and Required Reporting
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, compliance officer, Director of Nursing/Health Care Practitioner Supervisor, billing staff, and all employees
policies.purpose: To set up a corporate compliance program that gives staff a clear way to report suspected misconduct, violations of law or regulation and unethical practices, ensures prompt investigation and corrective action, and ensures that safety concerns and legal violations are reported to licensing and regulatory agencies as the law requires.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Best Practices §IV, Corporate Compliance Policy 4 and Best Practices §IV, Corporate Compliance Policy 7.

Corporate Compliance Policy 4 – Response to reports of misconduct, violations of law or regulation and unethical practices: [AGENCY NAME] has a written procedure, set out below, for receiving, logging, investigating and resolving every report, whether made by a client, family member, employee or other person and whether made orally, in writing or anonymously. Every report is taken seriously and is reviewed by the compliance officer within 2 business days. Corrective action is taken and documented. Reporters are protected from retaliation (see ADM-07).

Corporate Compliance Policy 7 – Reporting of safety concerns and violations of law to licensing and/or regulatory agencies, as required by law: [AGENCY NAME] reports safety concerns and violations of law to the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, the NJ Board of Nursing, law enforcement, state or county adult protective services, the Medicaid program or managed care organization, and any other agency, whenever a law, regulation, contract or accreditation standard requires it. The Administrator decides on reporting, with the governing body informed. Reporting is never delayed or withheld to protect the agency's reputation.

The agency appoints a compliance officer. It performs billing integrity audits of Medicaid claims. It prohibits false claims, kickbacks and inducements for referrals (federal False Claims Act, 31 USC 3729; federal Anti-Kickback Statute, 42 USC 1320a-7b). It files its annual financial statement with the Division of Consumer Affairs as required by N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5A, including any required audit or CPA review, and reports Medicaid PCA revenue accurately. It places aides only to perform tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.7). Training on fraud and abuse prevention is part of the annual in-service (see PER-07).

definitions.definition: Any act or omission that violates law, regulation, agency policy, a professional standard or the agency's code of conduct, including falsified records, billing for services not delivered, abuse or neglect, and acting outside delegated tasks.
Conduct that is contrary to professional ethics or agency policy even if not clearly illegal, such as accepting kickbacks, misleading clients, or conflicts of interest.
The person appointed by the governing body to run the compliance program: [COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME].
A scheduled review comparing claims to authorizations, visit records, EVV data and timesheets to confirm that every claim is accurate and supported.
A claim for payment to a government program, including Medicaid, that the agency knows is false or fraudulent or that it submits with reckless disregard of its truth.

procedures: The governing body appoints a compliance officer in writing and records the appointment in the minutes. The compliance officer reports directly to the Administrator and has direct access to the governing body.

The compliance officer posts and distributes the reporting methods: telephone [PHONE], email [EMAIL], confidential mailbox at [ADDRESS], and a direct report to the Administrator. Staff may report anonymously.

Any employee who suspects misconduct, a legal violation or an unethical practice reports it to the compliance officer, the Administrator or the Director of Nursing right away, and in any event within 24 hours of learning of it. Employees need not be sure a violation occurred before reporting.
Any person who receives a report logs it the same day on the compliance report log with date, source, summary and urgency, and passes it to the compliance officer.
Reports involving imminent danger to a client or abuse, neglect or exploitation are handled immediately under SAF-01 and SAF-02. The Director of Nursing takes steps to protect the client at once.
The compliance officer acknowledges receipt to the reporter (if known) within 2 business days and opens an investigation file.

The compliance officer investigates promptly, interviewing witnesses, reviewing records (client records, visit notes, EVV data, timesheets, claims), and preserving documents. Anyone implicated is kept out of the investigation. The investigation is normally completed within 30 days, and longer investigations are explained in the file.

The compliance officer writes findings, a conclusion (substantiated, not substantiated or inconclusive) and recommended corrective action. The Administrator reviews it and approves the action, such as retraining, discipline up to termination, repayment of overpayments or system changes.
Corrective action is documented with dates and assigned owners, and the compliance officer verifies completion. Discipline is applied consistently.

The Administrator decides within 5 business days of a substantiated finding whether a report to an outside agency is required. Reports are made to the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs ((973) 504-6370), the NJ Board of Nursing for a CHHA or nurse (973-504-6430), adult protective services or law enforcement, the Medicaid program, MCO or other payer, or other agencies, within the time required by the law or contract involved. Report content, date, recipient and confirmation are kept in the file.
If an overpayment or billing error is identified, the compliance officer works with billing staff to stop further claims, quantify the error, correct and refund the payer, and document the process.

Billing staff and the compliance officer conduct billing integrity audits of Medicaid claims (NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS and PPP) at least quarterly on a random sample, comparing the claim with the authorization, the plan of care, EVV or timekeeping data and the aide's weekly activity record (see CLN-07 and CLN-12). Results go to the Administrator and the quality assurance committee.

The Administrator ensures the annual financial statement for the prior calendar year is prepared to match the agency's State tax filing and is filed with the Division by July 1 and with the registration renewal, showing assets, liabilities, gross income, operating expenses and money received for NJ Medicaid PCA services. The Administrator confirms with the Division whether an audit or CPA-reviewed report is required for the year, based on PCA revenue and gross income (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.5A), and keeps the filing and proof of submission (see ADM-02).

The agency does not offer, pay, solicit or accept any payment or other benefit in return for client referrals or for ordering Medicaid-covered services, and does not submit or cause a claim to be submitted for services not delivered or not authorized.
Human resources checks each new hire and current employee against exclusion lists as required by PER-10. The compliance officer investigates any match at once.

Fraud and abuse prevention training is given at orientation (PER-06) and in the annual in-service (PER-07) and includes how to report concerns, the protections in ADM-07 and the laws cited in this policy. Attendance is recorded.
The compliance officer gives the governing body a written summary of reports, investigations, audits, refunds and external reports at least quarterly and reviews this policy annually (see ADM-14).

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the compliance officer, oversees the compliance program and receives quarterly reports.
Receives and logs reports, conducts investigations, leads billing integrity audits, and arranges training and external reporting with the Administrator.
Approves corrective action, decides on and makes required reports to licensing and regulatory agencies, and ensures financial filings are timely and accurate.
